France earlier summoned Iran's envoy and warned of a response (Reuters, AFP). NBC News describes the October hacks as among the most disruptive cyberattacks of the Iran war.
Europe.status: Attribution by French government; Iran denies; diplomatic dispute ongoing; no new attack reported; Belgian news agency Belga headlines "indications of Iranian involvement" in a cyber attack on refrigeration systems; Belga reports Tehran denies Iranian involvement in cyberattacks on Belgian refrigeration facilities

Europe.title: UPDATE: Spain holds its first nationwide general strike in 14 years; unions report police charges at a Mercamadrid picket; central Madrid hit by a 3-hour-plus blackout
Europe.summary: Reuters reports workers across Spain are staging the first general strike in 14 years over housing, and Al Jazeera says tens of thousands joined the walkout over wages, housing and prices. The CCOO union in Madrid says it will file a criminal complaint after police charges and the detention of a worker at a picket at the Mercamadrid wholesale market. El País Madrid separately reports a blackout of more than three hours across whole streets in central Madrid; its cause was not stated in the post checked.
Europe.status: Ongoing nationwide labour action; picket incident per union; blackout cause not stated, no link to the strike established; AFP says protesters disrupted the morning commute for hundreds of thousands of people; IGR Media reports violent clashes between protesters and riot police in Madrid, with police using batons and tear gas and detaining several demonstrators (single-account report of the clashes); Evening update: El Mundo reports looting and barricades in Barcelona and police charges in Madrid at the end of the strike, with 72 people detained across Spain; Al Arabiya reports protesters in Barcelona set bins on fire and threw projectiles at riot police, who responded with rubber bullets; Catalan News reports fires across Barcelona's city centre after the closing march; RTVE, citing the Government Delegation, reported two arrests in Madrid earlier in the evening; CBS News and The Daily Star report police fired tear gas during sporadic clashes in Madrid and Barcelona on Wednesday evening; Euronews reports riot police clashed with masked protesters in Madrid and Barcelona and more than 70 people were arrested; Al Arabiya says about 120,000 marched in central Madrid; eNCA says police fired tear gas during sporadic clashes; Reuters says millions joined the housing strike and scores were arrested in clashes with police; Novara Media footage shows riot police charging crowds in Barcelona, where workers set up roadblocks; AFP says the Spanish parliament passed measures restricting evictions on Thursday

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Car bomb kills a Russian Air Force colonel in Shushary, St. Petersburg
Russia.summary: A Russian military colonel was killed on the morning of Nov. 12 when an explosive device attached under his car detonated on Kolpinskoye Highway in the Shushary area of St. Petersburg as he drove out of a residential courtyard, the @charter_97 news account and multiple monitoring accounts report. Russian media cited by these accounts identify him as the chief navigator of the 6th Air Force and Air Defense Army, but he has not been named. It is the second similar under-car bombing of an officer in the same area since late August.

Russia.location: Omsk, Omsk Oblast, Russia (Gazprom Neft Omsk refinery)

NOELreports, Liveuamap, Exilenova+ and NEXTA report the refinery is on fire, with footage of a very large blaze. The refinery is roughly 2,500 km from the front line.

Russia.summary: Ukrainian state news agency Ukrinform was hit by a cyberattack on Nov. 11: hackers defaced its website and altered its official X profile, replacing its name and imagery with anti-Ukrainian propaganda, Hromadske reports. Russia.status: Confirmed by Ukrinform's director general per MTI; investigation under way; no attribution announced in posts checked; carried forward from 10:15 AM ET, no newer change found

Europe.status: Single established outlet found on X; no injuries reported; no Garda statement found; carried forward from 8:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Europe.title: CONTINUATION: Storm Charles — Portugal shuts schools and non-essential public services Wednesday; Web Summit day cancelled, UEFA youth matches postponed, Madeira flights cancelled
Europe.summary: Portugal announced the closure of schools and non-essential public services on Nov. 11 as Storm Charles brings red wind warnings, according to Itatiaia and elsalvador.com; elsalvador.com also reports the Web Summit conference was cancelled. UEFA postponed youth club and national-team matches scheduled in Portugal for Nov. 11, per FredLine. The UK Met Office had warned of strong winds followed by heavy rain across Madeira, Portugal and Spain, with flight disruption already reported in Madeira.
Europe.status: Government closure measures reported by multiple outlets; red warnings in place; claims of a formal "state of emergency" come only from individual accounts and are unconfirmed; no casualty reports found yet; Reuters reports Portugal cancelled more than 200 flights and shut schools as the storm hit; carried forward from 8:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: NEW: Russia launches a ballistic missile attack on Kyiv hours after the Abu Dhabi talks end; strikes reported in the city and Kyiv Oblast
Russia.location: Kyiv and Kyiv Oblast (Bila Tserkva, Irpin areas), Ukraine
Russia.summary: The Kyiv Independent says its journalists heard multiple explosions in Kyiv around 1 a.m. local time on Thursday (Nov. 12; about 6 p.m. ET Wednesday), shortly after Ukraine's Air Force warned that missiles were targeting the capital. OSINT account AMK Mapping says at least 11 missiles were used, including about five Iskander-Ms, and lists an Epicentr shopping center in northern Kyiv and the eastern industrial zone among the targets, with further strikes in the Bila Tserkva and Irpin areas. Journalist Oliver Carroll also reported ballistic strikes on Kyiv.
Russia.status: Early reports; casualties and damage not yet reported by Kyiv city or military administrations in posts checked; missile counts and targets come from an OSINT account and are unconfirmed

links.label: AMK Mapping: at least 11 missiles, targets listed

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Ukrainian drones attack the Omsk oil refinery in Siberia for hours; large fire reported at Russia's largest refinery
Russia.location: Omsk, Omsk Oblast, Russia (Gazprom Neft Omsk refinery)
Russia.summary: Russian local channels and multiple OSINT and media accounts report a prolonged Ukrainian drone attack on Omsk on Nov. 11, with the Gazprom Neft refinery named as the target and air defense activity lasting more than two hours. NOELreports, Liveuamap, Exilenova+ and NEXTA report the refinery is on fire, with footage of a very large blaze. The refinery is roughly 2,500 km from the front line.
Russia.status: Multiple independent accounts and footage; no official Russian statement on damage found in posts checked; Hromadske reports the Omsk regional governor confirmed a drone attack on the region but did not acknowledge a refinery strike; damage remains unclear; carried forward from 8:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Hackers deface Ukraine's state news agency Ukrinform and hijack its X account
Russia.summary: Ukrainian state news agency Ukrinform was hit by a cyberattack on Nov. 11: hackers defaced its website and altered its official X profile, replacing its name and imagery with anti-Ukrainian propaganda, Hromadske reports. The website was taken offline for maintenance as Ukrainian cybersecurity authorities investigated. Hungary's MTI says Ukrinform director general Serhiy Cheravatyi disclosed the attack.
Russia.status: Confirmed by Ukrinform's director general per MTI; investigation under way; no attribution announced in posts checked; carried forward from 8:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Russian strike on a crowded market in Chornomorsk, Odesa region, kills three and injures 11
Russia.summary: A Russian strike hit a market in central Chornomorsk on Nov. 11, killing three people and injuring 11, according to regional authorities cited by NOELreports and Ukrainian outlets. Hromadske Radio says nine of the injured were hospitalized, four in serious condition, and trading stalls were damaged and windows blown out. Early reports gave one dead before the toll rose.
Russia.status: Regional authorities report; toll rose from one to three killed during the morning; carried forward from 8:15 PM ET, no newer change found

links.label: New Voice of Ukraine on X

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Russian strike on a critical infrastructure enterprise in Dnipro kills three and injures four
Russia.summary: Suspilne, citing regional military administration head Oleksandr Hanzha, reports a Russian strike hit a critical infrastructure enterprise in Dnipro, killing two people, injuring at least four and starting a fire. Hromadske Radio later reported the toll rose to three, with businesses and a private home also damaged and four men hospitalized, two in serious condition. CGTN Europe, citing Ukraine's health service, reports three killed and five injured across Dnipropetrovsk region during the day.
Russia.status: Official (regional military administration) figures relayed by Ukrainian outlets; emergency services at the scene; facility not named; carried forward from 8:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Russian missile and drone strikes target Odesa Oblast bridges and 330 kV substations, plus substations in Kharkiv and Chernihiv, OSINT mapper reports
Russia.location: Odesa Oblast (Mayaky, Zatoka, Artsyz), Kharkiv and Chernihiv, Ukraine
Russia.summary: AMK Mapping reports a large combined Russian attack on Odesa Oblast overnight using cruise missiles, glide bombs and drones, targeting the Mayaky and Zatoka road bridges that link southern Odesa Oblast to the rest of Ukraine, as well as 330 kV substations in Artsyz and the "Podilska" substation. It says at least four cruise missiles were shot down and two flew briefly through Moldovan airspace. The same account reports fires in Kharkiv and Chernihiv after strikes on 110 kV substations.
Russia.status: Early reports; single OSINT mapping source; damage and outages not yet confirmed by Ukrainian officials or utilities on X; Kharkiv and Chernihiv substation strikes echoed by other OSINT accounts (one says one person injured in Kharkiv); still no Ukrainian official or utility statement found on X; First Squawk relays the Odesa governor saying energy targets were hit overnight; bne IntelliNews reports Russian strikes cut power to 135,000 in Odesa region; carried forward from 8:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Reuters says Russia pounds Ukraine's power grid as talks open in Abu Dhabi; Dnipro and Kyiv supply remains especially difficult
Russia.location: Dnipropetrovsk region (Dnipro, Pavlohrad, Kamianske and other communities), Ukraine; also Kharkiv and Zhytomyr regions
Russia.summary: Ukrinform reports Energy Minister Denys Shmyhal said the power supply situation remains especially difficult in Kyiv and Dnipro. NV reports President Zelensky raised the difficult electricity, water and heating situation in Kyiv, Dnipro and Kherson with European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen. Zelensky said earlier that more than 600,000 customers in the Dnipropetrovsk region were without power at the peak after strikes, and that supply was gradually being restored. Ukraine's Center for Strategic Communications says Russian forces attacked four districts of the Dnipropetrovsk region more than 20 times overnight.
Russia.status: Ongoing grid attacks per Reuters; restoration continuing; no current national outage total given; carried forward from 8:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Kryvyi Rih — AMK Mapping says two 330 kV substations hit by at least 16 Geran-2 drones; Reuters confirms partial blackout
Russia.summary: A massed Russian drone attack on energy infrastructure left parts of Kryvyi Rih without power, according to city official Oleksandr Vilkul. Apartment buildings, schools and kindergartens were damaged. Water and sewage services are being stabilized with generators, but heating will be harder to restore. AMK Mapping says at least 16 Geran-2 drones were used and that the "Pivdenna" and "Hirnycha" 330 kV substations on the city's southern outskirts were hit.
Russia.status: Official statement issued (city official Oleksandr Vilkul); Reuters reports the outage; substation details from OSINT mapping account, not officially confirmed; casualty figures not reported; Reuters headline reconfirmed this window; carried forward from 8:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Leningrad governor confirms fire in Ust-Luga port area and emergency substation shutdown during drone attack; says 146 drones intercepted overnight
Russia.summary: Leningrad region governor Alexander Drozdenko said a fire broke out in the Ust-Luga port area during an overnight Ukrainian drone attack and that a substation in the port zone went into emergency shutdown. He said 146 drones were intercepted over the region as of 7:30 a.m. local time and that there was no information on casualties. Earlier OSINT footage showed the oil terminal burning.
Russia.status: Official statement issued (Leningrad governor, relayed by OSINT/news accounts); no casualty information; extent of terminal damage unknown; tanker damage claims unconfirmed; NASA FIRMS satellite data shows multiple fires at and just off the port (OSINTdefender); Estonian public broadcaster ERR shows the fire visible from Estonia; Reuters carries the governor's account of the fire; Hromadske cites the governor on a substation shutdown and three injured workers; Meduza says two people were killed in the Smolensk region when officials say drone debris hit an apartment building; NOELreports says the Ust-Luga port terminal was still burning on Wednesday morning after the overnight attack; NOELreports cites OSINT channel Absreliable reporting fires at three 30,000-cubic-meter tanks and damage to processing equipment and a berth at Novatek; Russian sources cited by Osint613, OSINTdefender and NOELreports say two Ka-52 attack helicopters and an Mi-8 went down while responding to the drone attack, reportedly partly to friendly air defense, with one to three crews killed (Russian-source claims, unconfirmed by officials); Ukraine's SBU says the overnight operation struck port and oil infrastructure at Ust-Luga, damaging several petroleum storage tanks, and also hit the Buyan-M-class missile ship Naro-Fominsk; damage to the ship not established; carried forward from 8:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Reuters says Ukrainian strikes have cut Russia's oil refining capacity by about 30%; fuel purchase limits spread to St. Petersburg and Leningrad region
Russia.summary: The Kyiv Independent and Novaya Gazeta Europe, citing Reuters and two industry sources, report renewed Ukrainian attacks since late October have cut Russian refining capacity by about 30%, disrupting nine of Russia's 35 major refineries over the past week, including plants in Ryazan and Yaroslavl, per Meduza. SOTA, citing Bumaga, reports Rosneft stations in St. Petersburg have capped purchases since Nov. 8, and Novaya Gazeta Europe reports fuel limits returning in Leningrad region.
Russia.status: Refining capacity cut reported by Reuters (via established outlets); regional rationing reported; no official nationwide measure; carried forward from 8:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Railway bridge span collapses over the Viled River in Russia's Arkhangelsk region, derailing freight cars and halting traffic
Russia.summary: Meduza reports a span of a railway bridge collapsed in the Arkhangelsk region and several passenger trains were delayed. NEXTA reports several freight cars derailed after a section of the bridge over the Viled River collapsed between Cheryomukha and Viled and rail traffic on the section was suspended. Posts on X claim sabotage, but no official cause has been established.
Russia.status: Traffic halted on the section; at least eight passenger trains delayed per reports; cause under investigation; sabotage claims unverified; carried forward from 8:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.location: Kirovohrad, Kyiv, Dnipropetrovsk and other regions, Ukraine
Russia.summary: Ukraine's Center for Strategic Communications says air defenses neutralized 135 of 162 Russian drones, 70 of them jet-powered, and that Russia also launched an Iskander-M ballistic missile. It says hits were recorded in 19 locations and debris fell in nine more. It reports critical infrastructure in the Kirovohrad region was attacked, with two people injured, and that a business in Dnipro caught fire. Ukrainska Pravda and Ukrinform carry the same figures.
Russia.status: Daily casualty figures via Kyiv Independent; damage assessments continuing; Kyiv Independent's latest daily update repeats 9 killed and 39 injured and says two Russian cruise missiles violated Moldovan airspace; it says Russia launched a Kh-59/69 missile and 163 long-range drones overnight; carried forward from 8:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.summary: The head of the Sumy Regional Military Administration, Oleh Hryhorov, says a Russian drone deliberately struck a commuter train at the Sumy railway station on Tuesday morning. He says there were no passengers on board, the crew was in a shelter and there were no casualties. Ukrainska Pravda and RBC-Ukraine also report the attack on the train.
Russia.status: Official (regional military administration) statement; no casualties; damage to rolling stock; carried forward from 8:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Russian drones kill two in Ladyzhyn, Vinnytsia region; energy facilities and a civilian enterprise hit; three days of mourning
Russia.summary: Ukrainska Pravda reports that Russian forces attacked a civilian enterprise in Vinnytsia region, killing two people. The type of enterprise and the extent of the damage were not given in the post.
Russia.status: Reported by Kyiv Post and Ukrainska Pravda; energy damage extent not given; carried forward from 8:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Drones target military aircraft repair plant in Russia's Novgorod region; explosions reported near Staraya Russa
Russia.location: Staraya Russa, Novgorod Oblast, Russia; Crimea
Russia.summary: The Kyiv Independent reports explosions near the 123rd Aircraft Repair Plant in Staraya Russa, citing Telegram monitoring channels, as drones also targeted occupied Crimea. No damage assessment or official Russian or Ukrainian statement was found. RBC-Ukraine and Ukrinform, citing media reports, say drones targeted a plant in Novgorod region that services military aircraft.
Russia.status: Early reports; Ukrainian outlets citing media and monitoring channels; damage not officially confirmed on X; carried forward from 8:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Centrenergo warns of 'extremely serious' consequences after Russian strike on Trypillia Thermal Power Plant
Russia.summary: Russian forces struck the Trypillia Thermal Power Plant, the Kyiv Independent reports. Centrenergo, Ukraine's state-owned generating company, said the impact appears significant, but the extent of the damage is not yet clear and needs further inspection.
Russia.status: Operator statement issued (Centrenergo, via Kyiv Independent); damage assessment pending; no outage figures yet; carried forward from 8:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: IAEA says a Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant worker and a nearby thermal power plant employee were killed by drones
Russia.location: Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant, Enerhodar, Ukraine (Russian-occupied)
Russia.summary: The Kyiv Independent, citing the IAEA, reports a drone strike killed a worker at the Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant and that in a separate incident an employee at the nearby Zaporizhzhia Thermal Power Plant was also killed by a drone. Responsibility is not established in the posts found.
Russia.status: Official statement issued (IAEA, via Kyiv Independent); carried forward from 8:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Footage shows Ukrainian long-range drones striking the Morozov Plant in Russia's Leningrad region, followed by an emergency power outage
Russia.summary: NOELreports says Russian S-400 air defences fired at Ukrainian long-range drones during a Nov. 9 strike on the Morozov Plant in the Leningrad region, and that footage shows drones arriving one after another, with impacts followed by an emergency power outage. Russian- and Ukrainian-language channels carry the same footage and date it preliminarily to Nov. 9.
Russia.status: Footage-based OSINT reports; date preliminary; no official Russian confirmation found; carried forward from 8:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Russia.title: CONTINUATION: Yandex says 2.84% of Yandex Cloud customer data is permanently lost after October drone strikes on its data centers
Russia.summary: Reuters reports Yandex says nearly 3% of cloud customer data was lost after attacks. Yandex says it restored 97.16% of client data, but the rest is unrecoverable because equipment was critically damaged and those customers had no backups. It says backup will now be on by default.
Russia.status: Company statement relayed by Reuters and others; refers to October strikes; no new attack reported; carried forward from 8:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: NEW: Houthi ballistic missiles hit Al-Buraiqa district in Aden; Yemeni government condemns the attack
Middle East.summary: Al Mayadeen, citing local media in Aden, reports that a ballistic missile strike hit several sites in the Al-Buraiqa district west of Aden on Wednesday (Nov. 11), and Yemen Newsroom reports two powerful explosions in the city. The Houthi military spokesman claimed the missiles targeted a Saudi-led coalition command headquarters and operations room in Al-Buraiqa. Yemeni Information Minister Salem al-Awlaqi condemned the repeated shelling of Aden, most recently Al-Buraiqa, as targeting civilians, Al-Thawrah Net reports.
Middle East.status: Early reports; casualty claims (including reports of Saudi officers killed) come from partisan or unverified accounts and are not confirmed; no Saudi-led coalition statement found on X in posts checked

Middle East.location: Nasser Medical Complex, western Khan Younis, southern Gaza
Middle East.summary: Al Jazeera English reports at least four Palestinians were killed in an Israeli air attack on the Nasser Medical Complex in western Khan Younis on Wednesday evening (Nov. 11), citing Gaza Civil Defence spokesperson Mahmoud Basal. The Cradle, citing the same spokesperson, reports at least five killed and more than 20 injured, including a surgeon, and extensive damage to the surgical ward.
Middle East.status: Early reports; casualty figures from Gaza Civil Defence; no Israeli military statement found on X in posts checked; carried forward from 8:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: South Pars SPD14D platform fire extinguished; Al Jazeera says 17 workers jumped into the sea to escape
Middle East.location: South Pars gas field (Phase 14), Persian Gulf, Bushehr province, Iran
Middle East.summary: Iran International and Al Arabiya, citing Fars, report a fire broke out on a platform in Iran's South Pars gas field and the platform was evacuated, with Iran's deputy oil minister saying the situation is completely under control. Al Arabiya says the cause is under investigation and the platform produces about 14.5 million cubic meters of gas a day. Pars Oil and Gas Company, as relayed by an energy analyst, says the fire was contained. Claims on X of a US airstrike are not supported by any official or established source found.
Middle East.status: Official statement issued (Iranian deputy oil minister, via Fars); Reuters and Al Jazeera report the fire is out; no deaths reported in the posts found; cause not established; carried forward from 8:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: ADNOC Logistics & Services says one of its vessels was damaged in an attack inside UAE territorial waters
Middle East.summary: The National reports an Emirati ship operated by ADNOC Logistics & Services was attacked and damaged inside UAE territorial waters on Tuesday afternoon, and the company says response efforts are ongoing with further updates to follow. Anadolu, Emirati broadcaster ARN and gCaptain also report the attack. The vessel, the attacker and any casualties have not been identified in the posts.
Middle East.status: Company confirmation relayed by multiple established outlets; attacker not identified; casualties not reported; response ongoing; carried forward from 8:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: UKMTO says a tanker was struck by an unknown projectile 19 nautical miles northeast of Lima, Oman
Middle East.location: Strait of Hormuz, off Lima, Oman
Middle East.summary: Al Arabiya English reports, citing the UK Maritime Trade Operations agency, that a tanker reported being struck by an unknown projectile 19 nautical miles northeast of Lima, Oman. UKMTO issued warning 201-26 on the incident. gCaptain reports the strike alongside the ADNOC vessel attack in UAE waters. Damage and the attacker were not given in the posts.
Middle East.status: Official maritime advisory issued (UKMTO 201-26); attacker unidentified; damage assessment pending; carried forward from 8:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Reuters-verified videos show the Singapore-flagged tanker Navig8 Messi burning off the coast of Oman
Middle East.summary: Al Arabiya English says Reuters-verified videos released Nov. 8 and 9 show the Singapore-flagged tanker Navig8 Messi on fire off Oman. The cause and any casualties are not stated in the post.
Middle East.status: Video verification via Reuters, relayed by Al Arabiya; cause not stated; link to IRGC tanker claims or UKMTO advisories unconfirmed; carried forward from 8:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Oil slick off Oman and the UAE estimated at about 288 square km; Khor Fakkan shuts a beach
Middle East.location: Gulf of Oman, off Oman and the UAE (Khor Fakkan, Sharjah)
Middle East.summary: NEXTA reports Reuters has published satellite images showing large oil slicks off Oman and the UAE, with experts estimating the spill at about 288 square kilometres. Insurance Marine News and TradeWinds report the UAE city of Khor Fakkan shut a beach after detecting the spill. The source of the oil is not established in the posts.
Middle East.status: Environmental impact; source not officially identified; Reuters imagery relayed second-hand; carried forward from 8:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: Philippines confirms a Filipino seafarer was killed in a Nov. 5 drone attack on the tanker Velos Sapphire in the Persian Gulf
Middle East.location: Persian Gulf (vessel bound for Sitrah, Bahrain)
Middle East.summary: The Philippine Department of Migrant Workers says one Filipino crew member was killed and 21 others survived after the Greek-operated tanker Velos Sapphire was attacked on November 5. The Philippine News Agency says DMW Secretary Hans Leo Cacdac confirmed it was a drone attack. Remains and surviving crew are being repatriated.
Middle East.status: Official statement issued (DMW); attacker not identified in the posts; carried forward from 8:15 PM ET, no newer change found

Middle East.title: CONTINUATION: IRGC claim that two tankers burned in Hormuz, one after hitting a mine, remains unverified
Middle East.summary: Al Arabiya, Al Hadath and Sky News Arabia report Iranian media saying two oil tankers caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz after hitting naval mines. Iran International reports the IRGC Navy said one was a supertanker that struck a mine and alleged the second was travelling under the protection of US fighter jets. Al Arabiya cites Tasnim as saying the tankers had switched off navigation and positioning systems.

Middle East.summary: Reuters reports the Houthi-run Saba news agency said Saudi strikes hit Sanaa early Tuesday, while the Saudi-led coalition reported intercepting Houthi missiles and drones. America.title: Ballot scanners failing across Westchester County polling places
America.summary: Westchester County says its Board of Elections is aware of an issue with the paper ballots that is stopping voting machines from accepting them at polling locations throughout the county. Voters are still filling out paper ballots, which poll workers are placing in secure emergency bags to be counted later. New York Attorney General Letitia James says her office is monitoring and in touch with state and local election boards, and NBC News and lohud report machines down at multiple sites, including White Plains. Al Jazeera English also reports the scanner failures and says ballots are being collected in emergency orange bags to be counted later. Rep. Lawler and others say the bags will be police-escorted to the Board of Elections after polls close at 9 p.m., New York's normal closing time. Update, unconfirmed: an unverified account posts that Westchester County Police will take about 90,000 sealed, unscanned ballots to the Board of Elections, to be unsealed tomorrow in front of watchers before counting. No official Westchester or Board of Elections post confirming that figure or timeline was found. Update: the RNC's election-integrity account says the unscanned ballots will go under police custody to the Board of Elections for central counting with watchers present, and that counting will begin no later than 11 a.m. Wednesday. That timing comes from a partisan account and hasn't been posted by the county or the Board of Elections on X. Update, midnight ET: a judge issued emergency rules for counting the unscanned ballots, Spectrum News NY1's Gloria Pazmino reports, and Examiner Media says Republicans and Democrats agreed to seek court approval for a supervised process to secure and count them. Deccan Chronicle, carrying a wire report, says the judge let officials move thousands of paper ballots to a secure county warehouse under police escort, where they will be scanned under party supervision, delaying the count in the competitive 17th Congressional District until Wednesday. News 12's Nicholas Zifcak, reporting from the Board of Elections in White Plains, says counting at the BOE facility on the Saw Mill Parkway starts Wednesday at 11 a.m., and lohud reports County Executive Ken Jenkins says the ballots will be counted. Figures of 332 sites and 250,000 ballots circulating on X come from partisan and unverified accounts and are not confirmed by the county or the Board of Elections. lohud reports provisional paper ballots have been delivered to the Westchester Board of Elections, and The Rye Record reports the board says it will begin counting the emergency-bag ballots at 11 a.m. Wednesday. Update, 6 AM ET: ABC7NY (verified) reports the delayed Westchester ballots have been counted, with Conley and Bennett declared winners; Rep. Lawler had conceded NY-17 to Cait Conley before 11 p.m. Tuesday, per multiple posts. Figures of up to 332 sites and 250,000 ballots still trace to partisan outlets and are not confirmed by the county or the Board of Elections.
America.status: Delayed ballots reported counted (ABC7NY); stabilizing, moving to routine coverage

Europe.summary: The Afyonkarahisar Governorship says eight people were killed and one seriously injured in armed attacks across rural İhsaniye on Thursday. Europe.title: Second wave of cyberattacks on supermarket refrigeration
Europe.location: Across Europe, including Belgium, Sweden, Germany, Romania and the UK
Europe.summary: FBI Cyber Branch and FBI San Diego (verified), with CISA, HHS, USDA and DOT, issued a joint fact sheet today warning that industrial refrigeration and cold-chain monitoring systems are being targeted globally across critical infrastructure, putting food and medicine inventory at risk. This follows the second wave of European supermarket refrigeration cyberattacks already logged as HIGH, plus the French EFS blood-service cold-storage intrusion via contractor Coolworld. The National (verified) covers who may be behind European blood-bank and supermarket cold-storage attacks. Organizations are urged to apply the mitigations and report suspicious activity to the FBI.

AMK Mapping separately logged continued large-scale Geran drone and cruise-missile attacks overnight (200+ drones), with targets including substations and power plants around Kyiv, Vinnytsia, Dnipro and elsewhere.

Iran's state news agency IRNA earlier reported five explosions on the island. Officials quoted in media describe the strike as a defensive response to Iranian surface-to-air fire on a US aircraft; CENTCOM has not issued a statement. An Israeli military spokesperson says Israel was not involved. On Nov 3, President Trump said the US carried out a "minor attack" in Iran overnight, claiming Iranian ships and planes were destroyed and insisting it was not a war, per Al Jazeera. Iran's security chief said the Strait of Hormuz would reopen only if the US met Iran's seven conditions. Later on Nov 3, Reuters, citing a Financial Times interview, reported Trump said the US has no immediate plan to strike Iran again.
Middle East.status: US strikes acknowledged by President Trump; damage and casualty claims not independently confirmed; no CENTCOM statement found

America.title: Ballot scanners failing across Westchester County polling places
America.summary: Westchester County says its Board of Elections is aware of an issue with the paper ballots that is stopping voting machines from accepting them at polling locations throughout the county. Voters are still filling out paper ballots, which poll workers are placing in secure emergency bags to be counted later. New York Attorney General Letitia James says her office is monitoring and in touch with state and local election boards, and NBC News and lohud report machines down at multiple sites, including White Plains. Al Jazeera English also reports the scanner failures and says ballots are being collected in emergency orange bags to be counted later. Rep. Lawler and others say the bags will be police-escorted to the Board of Elections after polls close at 9 p.m., New York's normal closing time. Update, unconfirmed: an unverified account posts that Westchester County Police will take about 90,000 sealed, unscanned ballots to the Board of Elections, to be unsealed tomorrow in front of watchers before counting. No official Westchester or Board of Elections post confirming that figure or timeline was found. Update: the RNC's election-integrity account says the unscanned ballots will go under police custody to the Board of Elections for central counting with watchers present, and that counting will begin no later than 11 a.m. Wednesday. That timing comes from a partisan account and hasn't been posted by the county or the Board of Elections on X. Update, midnight ET: a judge issued emergency rules for counting the unscanned ballots, Spectrum News NY1's Gloria Pazmino reports, and Examiner Media says Republicans and Democrats agreed to seek court approval for a supervised process to secure and count them. Deccan Chronicle, carrying a wire report, says the judge let officials move thousands of paper ballots to a secure county warehouse under police escort, where they will be scanned under party supervision, delaying the count in the competitive 17th Congressional District until Wednesday. News 12's Nicholas Zifcak, reporting from the Board of Elections in White Plains, says counting at the BOE facility on the Saw Mill Parkway starts Wednesday at 11 a.m., and lohud reports County Executive Ken Jenkins says the ballots will be counted. Figures of 332 sites and 250,000 ballots circulating on X come from partisan and unverified accounts and are not confirmed by the county or the Board of Elections. lohud reports provisional paper ballots have been delivered to the Westchester Board of Elections, and The Rye Record reports the board says it will begin counting the emergency-bag ballots at 11 a.m. Wednesday. Update, 6 AM ET: ABC7NY (verified) reports the delayed Westchester ballots have been counted, with Conley and Bennett declared winners; Rep. Lawler had conceded NY-17 to Cait Conley before 11 p.m. Tuesday, per multiple posts. Figures of up to 332 sites and 250,000 ballots still trace to partisan outlets and are not confirmed by the county or the Board of Elections.
America.status: Delayed ballots reported counted (ABC7NY); stabilizing, moving to routine coverage

Europe.summary: Le Canard enchaîné reports that on the night of Nov 1–2 hackers attacked a contractor of the Établissement français du sang (EFS), France's blood service, and heated cold rooms holding blood samples, set to stay at minus 30 degrees, up to 110 degrees. FrenchBreaches names the contractor as Coolworld and says the incident was detected in time with no reported operational impact. It resembles the refrigeration attacks on European supermarkets. Update, 8 PM ET Nov 4: ABC News reports no blood products were compromised. Update, midnight ET Nov 5: GB News reports hackers targeted French blood banks in the latest European refrigeration cyberattack, and ABC7 News Bay Area likewise reports the blood-bank site was hit but no blood products were compromised. Attribution remains unknown.
Europe.status: Multiple outlets; no blood products compromised per ABC/ABC7; no EFS statement found on X this sweep; attribution unknown

Europe.title: Moldova suspects a state actor behind cyberattack
Europe.summary: Moldova's prime minister told Euronews the government suspects a state actor is behind a cyberattack. The Euronews post does not detail which systems were hit; unverified posts claim government databases and citizens' ID data were compromised.
Europe.status: Official statement reported by Euronews; scope and attribution under investigation

Europe.title: Hoax bomb threats hit at least 27 European flights; fighter escorts and diversions
Europe.location: Europe-wide (Ireland, France, Italy, Austria, Czechia, Bulgaria, Poland, Spain and other routes)
Europe.summary: Reuters (verified) reports a second wave this week of hoax bomb threats hitting European airlines from Ireland to Bulgaria, with at least 25 flights making unplanned landings or receiving fighter escorts in its earlier tally; multiple secondary accounts citing Reuters now put Thursday's total at least at 27, including a KLM Amsterdam–Tel Aviv flight diverted for inspection in Bucharest. An Aer Lingus Dublin–Rome flight was diverted to a French military base. No explosives have been reported found. Ynet Global and economist Steve Hanke also cover the wave.
Europe.status: Ongoing hoax wave; no confirmed explosives; scale at least mid-20s per Reuters and secondary tallies

Europe.title: Violent cost-of-living and anti-government protests
Europe.summary: On Oct 31, masked rioters looted shops in Frankfurt, and German police fired water cannons at youths throwing Molotov cocktails. In Paris and elsewhere in France, police fired tear gas as hundreds of thousands marched against living costs and police violence. In Tirana, protesters threw Molotov cocktails and paving stones at police. Swiss paper Tages-Anzeiger says the riots also reached Switzerland over the weekend, with protests in Zurich. On Tuesday, French students marched through central Paris despite the authorities rejecting their route, Reuters reports, and DW says German officials are looking for those responsible for the Gen Z protest riots.
Europe.status: Confirmed by major outlets; further marches possible

Europe.title: Poland deploys counterterrorism police near Kaliningrad
Europe.summary: Poland has deployed police counterterrorism units near the Kaliningrad border after intelligence warnings of possible sabotage in the coming days, the Kyiv Independent reports, citing Polish media.

Europe.title: Latvia says drones violated its airspace
Europe.summary: Latvia believes one of two drones that violated its airspace was Russian and the other Ukrainian, Reuters reports.

Europe.title: Germany arrests suspected organizer of Starlink ground station arson in Poland
Europe.location: Reutlingen district, Germany / Wola Krobowska, Poland
Europe.summary: German special police arrested a Turkish national on Nov 3 suspected of ordering the Sept 23 arson attack on a Starlink ground station south of Warsaw, according to a report citing Stuttgart prosecutors. Two alleged perpetrators were arrested in October. Polish prosecutors suspect Russian intelligence involvement, which German authorities have not confirmed.
Europe.status: Arrest reported; investigation ongoing

Europe.title: Student protest in Paris defies ban; tear gas near the Panthéon
Europe.summary: teleSUR English reports hundreds of students defied a protest ban in Paris to demand more education funding and economic reforms, and police used tear gas during clashes near the Panthéon. More protests are planned for November 5.
Europe.status: Early reports; single outlet; no police or official figures found

Russia.summary: Large parts of Kyiv remain dark after repeated Russian strikes on energy infrastructure, with emergency cuts and long scheduled outages. NEXTA and journalist JP Lindsley report emergency power cuts in several districts after strikes, with scheduled outages elsewhere and recent water-supply problems. Anton Gerashchenko says a large part of the capital is in blackout with many residents also lacking water or heating. Denys Glushko reports some districts without electricity more than 20 hours a day and street lighting off across almost the entire city including the center.
Russia.status: Ongoing; multi-source corroboration Thursday evening (NEXTA, Gerashchenko, Glushko, Lindsley); water/heating hardship continuing

Russia.title: Beget, a major Russian web host, still largely offline after cloud-wiping cyberattack
Russia.summary: Beget, one of Russia's largest hosting providers (~540,000 .ru domains), reported a massive cyberattack beginning about 02:40 Moscow time on November 2 that wiped cloud servers and some backups. Network observers say on day four only a small share of the network is answering. Government and commercial clients are among those affected; full restoration timeline unclear.

Russia.title: Main gas pipeline explosion and fire in Topkinsky district, Kemerovo
Russia.location: Topki / Topkinsky district, Kemerovo Oblast, Russia (Siberia)
Russia.summary: On Nov. 5 a main gas transmission pipeline in the Topkinsky municipal district suffered depressurization, followed by a powerful explosion and large fire. Regional Governor Ilya Seredyuk confirmed the fire; later reports say the blaze was extinguished. Multiple accounts note this is the second major Russian trunk-pipeline fire in about a month (after a Penza-region incident around Oct. 13). Cause remains unclear; sabotage is speculated in some posts but not proven.
Russia.status: Confirmed by regional governor; fire reported extinguished; cause under investigation / unclear

Russia.title: Water outages across all Kyiv districts after emergency power cuts at the city water utility
Russia.summary: Kyivvodokanal facilities lost power again under emergency blackouts on November 5, disrupting water across all districts; Sota News says service is gradually being restored. Afternoon videos from Saint Javelin and Military Summary show a large-scale blackout across Kyiv, with some areas getting only a few hours of power and scheduled outage calendars failing. Zelenskyy said every Ukrainian power plant has been affected and appealed for transformers, cables and generators.
Russia.status: Ongoing; water gradually restoring; citywide blackout videos afternoon of Nov 5

Russia.location: Kyiv city; Kyiv, Zhytomyr, Chernihiv and Cherkasy oblasts; Sumy oblast, Ukraine
Russia.summary: OSINT account AMK Mapping says emergency power outages were imposed across Kyiv Oblast after overnight Russian jet-drone strikes on energy infrastructure, naming the Kyivska 750 kV substation and the Trypillia thermal power plant among the targets, with further emergency cuts in Zhytomyr, Chernihiv and Cherkasy oblasts and Kyiv city on top of rolling blackouts. Ukrainian outlet Blyskavka reports emergency shutdowns in parts of three Kyiv districts, across all of Sumy oblast, and in one Chernihiv district after a night attack on an energy facility. Accounts relaying Ukrenergo say scheduled outage timetables are not in force.

Russia.summary: An air raid siren sounded in Kyiv on Wednesday evening local time, and EuromaidanPR reported explosions in the city at about 3:24 PM ET and said air defense was active over Kyiv at about 3:53 PM ET. Casualty and damage figures had not been reported by officials on X at sweep time.
Russia.status: Early reports; attack ongoing at sweep time; no official damage or casualty figures

Russia.summary: The Kyiv Independent says it was hit by a suspected Russian cyberattack. Russia.title: Russian drone strike sets Odesa's 7th Kilometer market on fire
Russia.summary: Russian drones struck the 7th Kilometer market near Odesa, one of Ukraine's largest wholesale markets, on Wednesday morning, starting a large fire seen on video. One account says the strike came during the working day while the market was busy. No official casualty figures were found in the posts reviewed.
Russia.status: Early reports with video; casualties unknown

Russia.title: Ukrainian drone strike sets Ozon logistics hub in Adygeysk on fire
Russia.summary: A drone attack overnight on November 4 set fire to online retailer Ozon's logistics centre in Adygeysk, damaging the building and partially collapsing its roof, Militarnyi reports. Ozon confirmed the attack and said staff were evacuated, with no casualties reported, and the head of Adygea also confirmed it. Videos posted by OSINT accounts show a large fire at the site.

Russia.title: 310-drone overnight attack on Ukraine; Zhytomyr largely without power
Russia.location: Kyiv, Zhytomyr, Odesa and other regions, Ukraine
Russia.summary: Russia launched 310 drones overnight into November 4, according to Ukraine's Air Force as cited by journalist Michael Bociurkiw, targeting Kyiv, Dnipro, Poltava, Odesa, Ternopil and the Rivne and Kirovohrad regions. Hromadske Radio reports Zhytomyr remains largely without power after a strike, with electric transport suspended and water facilities on generators. Kyiv Post shows Kyiv in a blackout on generators, and Bociurkiw reports large parts of Odesa without power and Kyiv water only partly restored. Russia.title: Russian bombing kills 43 at aid point in Komyshuvakha; dozens still missing
Russia.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the death toll from a Russian strike on an aid point in Komyshuvakha (Zaporizhzhia region) has risen to 43, with Anadolu Agency and other outlets confirming the figure. Zelenskyy also said the toll could climb toward 100 as rescue work continues and dozens remain missing. The strike hit people who had gathered for aid including bread.

Russia.location: Odesa, Cherkasy, Zhytomyr, Vinnytsia, Kharkiv, Dnipro, Chernivtsi, Chernihiv and Rivne regions, Ukraine
Russia.summary: Mass Russian strikes on Ukraine's energy system on Nov. 3 triggered Kyiv's most severe water outage of the full-scale invasion, the Kyiv Independent reported citing three people with knowledge of the matter including a government advisor; Rob Lee amplified the report overnight. Residents across most Kyiv districts went more than 24 hours without water after power to pumping was cut. AMK Mapping separately logged continued large-scale Geran drone and cruise-missile attacks overnight (200+ drones), with targets including substations and power plants around Kyiv, Vinnytsia, Dnipro and elsewhere.
Russia.status: Confirmed water outage cascading from Nov. 3 grid strikes; drone campaign continuing

Zelenskyy told PBS NewsHour that Ukraine targeted Russia's emergency alert systems in a retaliatory hack. Middle East.summary: The Saudi-led coalition's spokesperson, Maj. Gen. Turki Al-Malki, said air defenses intercepted and destroyed a Houthi ballistic missile launched toward the Madinah region on Thursday, as reported by Saudi Gazette, Khaleej Times and Kuwait Times. Middle East.summary: Accounts citing the Shin Bet and Israeli police report that a 19-year-old East Jerusalem resident was arrested over a plan to detonate an explosive at Lions' Gate and then open fire on civilians and officers at the Temple Mount. Middle East.title: Houthi missile strike on Lahj health center kills five
Middle East.summary: A ballistic missile attributed to the Houthis hit the Al-Saqiya health center in Lahj, killing five people and injuring 15, including medical staff, according to Yemen's government-aligned forces and local outlets. Middle East.location: Al-Alalah camp, Qa'tabah district, Al Dhale, Yemen
Middle East.summary: Yemeni outlets report a ballistic missile strike attributed to the Houthis hit the Al-Alalah training camp for new recruits in Qa'tabah district on Wednesday morning. Middle East.title: US strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island
Middle East.location: Qeshm Island, Strait of Hormuz, Iran
Middle East.summary: A US official told Reuters that the US carried out strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz late Monday, Nov. 2. The Economic Times, citing The Wall Street Journal, says it is the latest in a series of limited, unpublicized US strikes in recent weeks. Iran's state news agency IRNA earlier reported five explosions on the island. Officials quoted in media describe the strike as a defensive response to Iranian surface-to-air fire on a US aircraft; CENTCOM has not issued a statement. An Israeli military spokesperson says Israel was not involved. On Nov 3, President Trump said the US carried out a "minor attack" in Iran overnight, claiming Iranian ships and planes were destroyed and insisting it was not a war, per Al Jazeera. Iran's security chief said the Strait of Hormuz would reopen only if the US met Iran's seven conditions. Later on Nov 3, Reuters, citing a Financial Times interview, reported Trump said the US has no immediate plan to strike Iran again.
Middle East.status: US strikes acknowledged by President Trump; damage and casualty claims not independently confirmed; no CENTCOM statement found

Africa.title: Two killed near voting stations after South Africa's local elections
Africa.location: Bushbuckridge, Mpumalanga, and Polokwane, Limpopo, South Africa
Africa.summary: Mpumalanga police say two unknown gunmen shot at a group celebrating outside a voting station in Boikhutso village, Bushbuckridge, while awaiting the vote count, killing a 57-year-old man; the motive is unknown. In Polokwane, police say a 31-year-old man was stabbed to death at about 5 AM local time in a park opposite the Florapark Comprehensive School voting station after an altercation between two people allegedly from the same political party; a 35-year-old suspect was arrested.
Africa.status: Police statements relayed; one suspect arrested in Polokwane; Bushbuckridge suspects sought

links.label: ZA News Flash: two deaths at election venues

Africa.title: Ballot papers stolen and voter intimidation reported in eThekwini on South Africa's local election day
Africa.location: eThekwini (Durban) and Hillcrest, KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa
Africa.summary: SABC News reports IEC Deputy CEO Masego Sheburi says a police case was opened after voting materials were stolen at Ward 2 in eThekwini, and that KwaZulu-Natal police are investigating a burglary in which ballot papers and other sensitive IEC materials were taken from a voting station in Hillcrest, west of Durban. Separately, video posted by MDN News appears to show MK Party supporters manhandling a man of Somali descent who presented a South African ID at a Durban voting station; that account has not been confirmed by the IEC or police in the posts reviewed. Voting elsewhere was reported as largely peaceful.
Africa.status: IEC says police case opened over stolen materials; intimidation video unconfirmed by officials

links.label: SABC News: IEC confirms police case
MDN News (verified): video of confrontation, unconfirmed

Africa.title: Peter Obi's convoy attacked in Calabar
Africa.summary: New Telegraph reports the convoy of NDC presidential candidate Peter Obi came under attack in Calabar after he visited the palace of the Obong of Calabar. Update, 8 PM ET: TheCable reports the Cross River State police command says suspected hoodlums armed with machetes and sticks attacked the convoy, and police have arrested one suspect. Injuries and damage have not been detailed in the posts reviewed.
Africa.status: Confirmed by police, per TheCable; one suspect arrested; investigation under way

links.label: TheCable: police confirm attack, arrest suspect

Africa.title: Johannesburg power outages on local election day
Africa.summary: City Power reported several faults on the morning of South Africa's local government elections, including an outage at Boothill Switching Station affecting Wilgeheuwel, Honeydew and nearby areas, and one at Mayfair Substation affecting Amalgam. Teams were on site investigating; some other outages, such as Orchards and Ennerdale, were fully or mostly restored. No impact on specific voting stations was reported in the posts reviewed.
Africa.status: Official statements issued by City Power; repairs ongoing

Africa.title: Dynamite blast at Ghana–Burkina Faso border kills immigration officer; curfew imposed
Africa.location: Hamile, Lambussie District, Upper West Region, Ghana
Africa.summary: A suspected load of dynamite on a tricycle exploded at Hamile on the Burkina Faso border early Tuesday, killing an immigration officer, according to several Ghanaian outlets. The Interior Ministry imposed a 6 PM to 5 AM curfew on Hamile and banned arms and ammunition. The district's chief executive said youths massed against immigration officers after the blast. Citi FM reports Muntaka urged chiefs and elders to calm agitated youth, and that the Ghana Immigration Service cautioned the public against circulating unverified reports. Update: the Ghanaian Times now reports at least three people dead and others critically injured in the suspected dynamite explosion in Hamile; earlier reports cited one immigration officer killed. The toll has not been confirmed in an official post reviewed. Update: Ghanaian Times reports at least three dead and others critically injured; an 11-hour daily curfew has been imposed in Hamile.
Africa.status: Official curfew issued; cause and full toll still being reported

links.label: Ghanaian Times: at least three dead
Citi FM: calls to calm youth
Citi FM: GIS warns on unverified reports

Africa.title: Mapleton power restored, but water outages continue in Gauteng-area municipalities
Africa.location: Ekurhuleni, Tshwane (Pretoria), Lesedi, Govan Mbeki, Victor Khanye and Thembisile Hani municipalities, South Africa
Africa.summary: The City of Ekurhuleni says power has been restored at the Mapleton substation that feeds Rand Water's Mapleton Pumping Station in Boksburg, after a failure that cut water to six municipalities including the Ekurhuleni and Tshwane metros. Parts of Thembisa and Tsakane still have low pressure or no water while reservoirs refill, and the city has sent water tankers. eNCA says Ekurhuleni's mayor expects the system to be fully restored overnight. Update, 6 AM ET: the City of Ekurhuleni says pumping has been restored but water supply remains constrained, with high-lying areas slower to recover.
Africa.status: Power and pumping restored; water supply still constrained in high-lying areas

links.label: City of Ekurhuleni (official): water still constrained

Africa.title: Bandits ambush police on Sokoto–Gusau highway
Africa.summary: Suspected bandits ambushed police officers traveling from Sokoto to Zamfara State for special duty, killing at least five, according to New Telegraph. Local outlets report some officers were abducted and say police confirmed the attack.
Africa.status: Confirmed by police, per local reports

Africa.title: Explosion at Metafrique Steel plant in Douala
Africa.summary: An explosion at the Metafrique Steel plant killed at least four people and severely burned 16, the regional governor said. The cause is under investigation.
Africa.status: Official toll from regional governor; cause under investigation

Africa.title: Johannesburg water crisis
Africa.summary: Residents and civic activists planned a protest outside Johannesburg Water's head office, and the Joburg Crisis Alliance is threatening legal action against the city over unreliable water supply. The mayor says intensified technical work is beginning to improve supply. On Nov 3, the mayor said water storage across Johannesburg's system has improved to more than 41 percent, up from 37 percent over the weekend, per SABC News.
Africa.status: Improving per the mayor

Africa.title: MK Party organiser shot dead before KZN local elections
Africa.summary: MK Party regional organiser Lastborn Shazi was shot dead at his home in Umzumbe during preparations for South Africa's local government elections. KZN police spokesperson Col. Robert Netshiunda appealed for calm and asked the public to give police space to investigate the murder.
Africa.status: Police investigating; no arrests reported

Africa.title: At least eight killed in attack in Nigeria's Zamfara state
Africa.summary: CGTN Africa's bulletin reports at least eight people killed in an attack in Zamfara state. No details on attackers or location were given in the post.
Africa.status: Single-source report

Africa.title: Lagos Island residents protest days-long power outages
Africa.summary: Residents of Lagos Island took to the streets to protest a prolonged lack of electricity in their communities, according to Silverbird Television.
Africa.status: Early reports; single outlet

Africa.title: Suspected RSF drone strike kills seven in South Kordofan
Africa.summary: CGTN Africa reports seven people killed in a suspected RSF drone strike in South Kordofan. Details on the target were not given.
Africa.status: Single outlet

Africa.title: Al-Shabab attack on army position near Xarardheere
Africa.summary: A Somali news account reports a heavy Al-Shabab attack early Wednesday on a federal military position at Faax. Casualties among government forces are reported but unconfirmed, and it is unclear whether the position was overrun.
Africa.status: Early, single-source report

Africa.title: Al-Shabab bombing kills two AU soldiers in Jowhar
Africa.summary: A local Somali outlet reports two Burundian AUSSOM soldiers were killed and three Somali soldiers wounded when Al-Shabab targeted a joint foot patrol in Jowhar with an explosive device on Wednesday afternoon.
Africa.status: Single local source; no AUSSOM or government statement found on X

Africa.title: Ethiopian clashes spill bombs and gunfire into Moyale, Kenya
Africa.summary: NTV Kenya reports military bomb experts detonated at least seven unexploded bombs and recovered dozens of live rounds fired into Moyale, Kenya, from Moyale, Ethiopia, as two weeks of Oromo-Somali clashes spill across the border.
Africa.status: Established Kenyan broadcaster; casualty figures not given

Africa.title: RSF drone attack on Damazin, Blue Nile state
Africa.summary: SNT24 reports the Blue Nile regional government condemned an RSF drone attack on Damazin that hit residential areas and civilian infrastructure and caused civilian casualties. No casualty figures or independent confirmation were found this sweep.
Africa.status: Official condemnation reported by a single outlet; toll unknown

Africa.title: Gunmen attack market in Benue State's Logo LGA
Africa.location: Abeda Shitile, Logo LGA, Benue State, Nigeria
Africa.summary: Gunmen attacked the Abeda Shitile community on Tuesday evening as traders were closing for the day, per a Nigerian news account. The Benue State Police Command reportedly confirmed three deaths and two injured, while community sources say four were killed and eight injured.
Africa.status: Single-source report citing police; tolls differ

South America.title: Paraguay: Ueno Bank seizure locks out ~3M; Peña resigns as Diputados approve juicio político
South America.summary: Paraguay’s central bank seized digital lender Ueno Bank, locking roughly three million customers (~60% of adults) out of accounts and sparking protests. Insider Paper (verified) reports President Santiago Peña resigned amid the fallout and says he will attend an impeachment trial. Bloomberg en Español (verified) and Il Sole 24 Ore cover the collapse leaving millions without savings access and the resulting political crisis. Diputados had moved toward juicio político over Peña's prior ties to the ownership group.
South America.status: Resignation confirmed; impeachment path active; deposit lockout ongoing

links.label: Insider Paper (verified): Peña resigns; will attend trial
Il Sole 24 Ore: Peña resigns after Ueno chaos
LatAm briefing: scale and political ties

South America.title: Heavy fighting between Colombian Army and FARC dissidents in Timba, Valle del Cauca
South America.location: Timba, Buenos Aires municipality, Valle del Cauca, Colombia
South America.summary: NTN24 and DiariOriente report strong clashes Thursday between the Colombian Army and alleged Jaime Martínez FARC dissidents under alias Iván Mordisco in rural Timba. Video circulated of the firefight. Casualties were not confirmed in the cited posts.
South America.status: Early media reports; casualties not confirmed in cited posts

South America.title: Tornado damages Chapecó airport; all flights suspended
South America.summary: Santa Catarina's Civil Defense confirmed a tornado hit Chapecó on Wednesday morning, tearing structures off the Serafim Enoss Bertaso airport terminal and damaging other parts of the city. g1 reports gusts of 93 km/h at the state station and up to 126 km/h per the national weather institute (Inmet). Jovem Pan reports all takeoffs and landings are suspended indefinitely, with no injuries recorded so far.
South America.status: Official confirmation (Civil Defense); airport closed indefinitely; no injuries reported

links.label: Jovem Pan News: flights suspended indefinitely

South America.title: Truck bomb near police station on Pan-American Highway in Patía, Cauca
South America.summary: A dump truck loaded with explosives detonated about 500 meters from the El Estrecho police station on the Pan-American Highway on Wednesday, Noticias RCN and El Espectador report. El Tiempo and RCN give a preliminary toll of one dead and six injured, while President Abelardo De La Espriella said one civilian was killed and two women injured and ordered security forces to find those responsible. Blu Radio says the person killed was a 20-year-old barber, and the highway was closed. Update, 8 PM ET: several Colombian outlets report one civilian was killed and two women injured, and Canal 1 reports Abelardo de la Espriella condemned the attack. Early injury counts of up to six have not been confirmed.
South America.status: Official statement issued by the president; one civilian killed per several outlets; no claim of responsibility found

links.label: Canal 1: one dead, two women injured; president condemns
La Hora de la Verdad: one dead, two injured

South America.title: Explosive thrown at Media Canoa toll plaza in Valle del Cauca
South America.summary: Men on a motorcycle threw an explosive at the Media Canoa toll on the Cali–Buga road around 3:45 a.m. Wednesday, damaging two lanes, according to Revista Semana, El País Cali and BLU Radio, citing police. No injuries were reported. Police are seeking those responsible, and no group has claimed it.
South America.status: Reported by several established Colombian outlets citing police; no injuries

South America.title: Protests over power cuts in several Venezuelan cities
South America.location: Carabobo, Lara, Cojedes and Aragua states, Venezuela
South America.summary: Residents protested overnight over long power cuts in Los Guayos (Carabobo), Barquisimeto (Lara), Tinaco (Cojedes) and Maracay, according to local journalists and residents' posts, with some areas reportedly without power for up to 24 hours. No injuries or arrests were reported in the posts reviewed, and no statement from the electricity company Corpoelec was found.
South America.status: Early reports from local accounts; no established-outlet confirmation yet

South America.title: Truck bomb near military base in Planadas, Colombia
South America.summary: A truck loaded with explosives detonated near a military base in Planadas, Tolima, killing four civilians, including a two-month-old girl, an official said. The blast heavily damaged a hospital, a school and several homes, and reports citing Colombia's Defense Ministry put the injured at 17. Colombian authorities have named two FARC dissident commanders under alias Iván Mordisco as responsible, NTN24 reports, and residents held a candlelight vigil Tuesday evening. Revista Semana reports Planadas's mayor has asked for a speedy investigation into the attack.
South America.status: Confirmed by officials and major outlets; attributed by authorities to FARC dissidents

links.label: Revista Semana: mayor seeks swift investigation
NTN24 (verified): authorities name two dissident commanders
Diario El Salvador citing Colombia's Defense Ministry

South America.title: Second police officer dies after motorbike bomb in Algeciras, Huila
South America.summary: Colombia's National Police announced the death of a patrolman gravely wounded in Sunday's terrorist attack in Algeciras, Huila. Noticias Caracol reports he is the second police officer to die from the motorbike bomb.
South America.status: Official statement issued

South America.title: Drone attack kills two soldiers in Colombia's Chocó
South America.summary: DW Español reports two soldiers were killed and five wounded in a drone attack in a rural area of Chocó. It is the second explosives attack in Colombia in under 24 hours, after the Planadas truck bomb. Noticias RNN also reports a drone attack killing two soldiers and wounding five. Commentator Manuel Pedrero places a drone attack on the El Trapiche military post in Ocaña, Norte de Santander, and says authorities blamed the ELN; it is unclear whether that is the same attack, so the location is unresolved.
South America.status: Reported by an established outlet; no claim of responsibility seen

South America.title: Security breach halts Brazil's Mercado Bitcoin exchange
South America.summary: Mercado Bitcoin, one of Brazil's largest crypto exchanges, said it identified and contained a security incident in one of its systems overnight and suspended deposits and withdrawals as a precaution. In a later update it put the assets involved at about US$38 million and said about US$11 million had been frozen with partners including Tether and Circle. The exchange says customers will not lose assets and no data was leaked; services remained suspended with no restart time given.
South America.status: Official statement issued; services suspended

South America.title: Magnitude 5.6 earthquake in Tolima, Colombia
South America.summary: The Colombian Geological Service says a magnitude 5.6 earthquake struck at 4:13 a.m. local time on Nov 3 with its epicenter near Chaparral, Tolima, at a shallow depth of about 19 km. El Tiempo, citing the national disaster agency, says one person was injured, and Noticias Caracol reports a woman in Chaparral was hurt when a wall fell on her. El Tiempo also reports serious damage to homes in Chaparral based on social media video.
South America.status: Official statement issued by the Colombian Geological Service; damage assessment ongoing

South America.title: Protesters block Morón–Coro highway over power failures
South America.summary: Caraota Digital reports residents blocked the Morón–Coro highway in another protest over electrical failures, demanding answers from authorities.
South America.status: Single-source local report

South America.title: Colombian police say they foiled a bomb attack on a Pan-American Highway toll
South America.location: Nariño, Colombia, near the Ecuador border
South America.summary: UHN Plus reports that Colombia's president said police foiled an attack on a toll station on the Pan-American Highway in Nariño and found 117 kilos of explosives.
South America.status: Single source this sweep; no post from Colombian police or the presidency found on X

South America.title: Explosion and fire at Zulia substation reported to cut power
South America.location: Federación substation, Ciudad Ojeda, Zulia, Venezuela
South America.summary: An activist account reports a loud explosion followed by a fire at the Federación electrical substation in Ciudad Ojeda, leaving parts of Zulia without power. Scale and cause aren't known.
South America.status: Early reports; single non-official source; no statement from Corpoelec found

South America.title: Drone and rifle attack on police station in Chimichagua, Cesar
South America.summary: El Tiempo reports a drone and rifle attack on the police station in Chimichagua, Cesar, left no one injured. Noticias Caracol earlier reported a drone attack against police in Cesar department.
South America.status: Reported by two established outlets; no injuries reported

South America.title: US reportedly helped Venezuela in deadly strike on ELN in Apure
South America.summary: Infobae, carrying a New York Times report, says US officials say the US helped Venezuela carry out a lethal drone strike on an ELN guerrilla base in Apure. Casualty figures were not in the post.
South America.status: Reported by major outlet citing officials

South America.title: Ecuador's National Assembly website hit by cyber incident
South America.summary: An Ecuadorian outlet reports the National Assembly's official web portal was compromised on Wednesday, and the legislature activated containment protocols and asked the public not to share any unauthorized content posted while the site was compromised. The assembly has ordered a technical report; it has not said how long the breach lasted or whether internal systems or databases were accessed.
South America.status: Single outlet report of an official statement; scope unknown

threats.title: Low-priority log
threats.summary: Fraud and 'rigged' framing of the Westchester scanner failure, the Fulton County rescan and the Maricopa Laveen outage has no official support. Unverified posts claim the refrigeration attacks spread to 13 European countries and to US military installations. A 'Worldwide Alert' roundup from the Paul Gold Eagle account mixes real events with unsupported claims. A Florida 'state beach shooting' post from a low-credibility account appears to confuse the Moss Landing, California shooting and has no corroboration. Claims of an official 90-day blackout warning have no official source. Earlier unsupported claims (Jacksonville blackout, a successful Iranian strike on a US base in Kuwait, Russia hitting six power plants) still have no corroboration. Posts claiming widespread Pennsylvania scanner failures got a reply from the Pennsylvania Department of State saying scanner jams don't stop ballots from being counted and that it has no reports of widespread scanner issues. Viral 'Iran nuclear survival guide' and 'massive Iran internet blackout' posts come from low-credibility accounts; see the sourced internet-outage item instead. 7:30 PM sweep: viral video of multi-hour lines in Columbus, OH is circulating as Election Day footage, but replies identify it as past early-voting footage from the Franklin County Board of Elections site, so it was not logged. Unverified claims that Newaygo County, MI ran out of ballots and that Wayne County polls lost power just before closing found no official or verified-outlet support. Partisan 'cheating' framing around the Gibraltar threat was ignored. 8 PM sweep: a viral post claiming Wayne County polling places lost power remains unsupported beyond the single Canton Township report logged above; claims of a Mesa, AZ vote-center power closure 'per the Recorder's Office' still have no official source. New this sweep: a small account claims a 'BulkaHackers' arrest in Kosovo with no corroboration; posts framing Wayne County results as delayed countywide by fraud have no official support; posts claiming an Iranian missile barrage on Israel are contradicted in replies and by the lack of any official or major-outlet report; and PaulGoldEagle-style posts claiming more Ohio threats remain unsupported. New tonight: an unverified viral post claims a San Diego library ballot drop box overflowed and ballots were mishandled; the San Diego County Registrar has not addressed it on X, and it is not confirmed. A King County, WA 'voter fraud' video claim comes from a low-credibility account with no official support. Claims of a 'major power outage' on Colorado's Front Range are contradictory and have no utility or official source. Claims that Iran launched a massive hypersonic missile attack on Israeli bases come from low-credibility accounts and are not reported by the IDF or major outlets. 2:00 AM sweep: a new Paul Gold Eagle roundup lists Election Day voting disruptions across several states and frames them as deliberate interference without official confirmation; it is not logged as an alert. 4 PM sweep: a viral thread claiming hackers are hitting 'the world's money system in 7 places at once' was checked by another account, which found the incidents are separate, mostly already known, and include an ECB malware story it could only trace to 2019; it is not one coordinated attack. A post predicting a nationwide blackout this month has no source. Claims that the Paraguay banking crisis caused riots beyond the Asunción clashes logged above come from low-credibility accounts, and a Paraguay-based account calls a viral 'riots in Paraguay' video clickbait. 8 PM sweep: recurring posts claiming Election Day power outages were used to slip in fake ballots have no official or verified-outlet source and are not logged. 10 PM sweep: posts claiming a new White House shooting today recycle the May 23, 2026 checkpoint shooting, per a fact-check reply, and are not logged. A post claiming Netanyahu was seriously injured in an attack in Tel Aviv comes from a GESARA-branded account with no corroboration. Crypto-account framing of the Crédit Mutuel Arkéa breach as part of a coordinated attack on the global financial system remains unsupported.
threats.status: Unverified; not elevated

America.title: Ballot scanners failing across Westchester County polling places
America.summary: Westchester County says its Board of Elections is aware of an issue with the paper ballots that is stopping voting machines from accepting them at polling locations throughout the county. Voters are still filling out paper ballots, which poll workers are placing in secure emergency bags to be counted later. New York Attorney General Letitia James says her office is monitoring and in touch with state and local election boards, and NBC News and lohud report machines down at multiple sites, including White Plains. Al Jazeera English also reports the scanner failures and says ballots are being collected in emergency orange bags to be counted later. Rep. Lawler and others say the bags will be police-escorted to the Board of Elections after polls close at 9 p.m., New York's normal closing time. Update, unconfirmed: an unverified account posts that Westchester County Police will take about 90,000 sealed, unscanned ballots to the Board of Elections, to be unsealed tomorrow in front of watchers before counting. No official Westchester or Board of Elections post confirming that figure or timeline was found. Update: the RNC's election-integrity account says the unscanned ballots will go under police custody to the Board of Elections for central counting with watchers present, and that counting will begin no later than 11 a.m. Wednesday. That timing comes from a partisan account and hasn't been posted by the county or the Board of Elections on X. Update, midnight ET: a judge issued emergency rules for counting the unscanned ballots, Spectrum News NY1's Gloria Pazmino reports, and Examiner Media says Republicans and Democrats agreed to seek court approval for a supervised process to secure and count them. Deccan Chronicle, carrying a wire report, says the judge let officials move thousands of paper ballots to a secure county warehouse under police escort, where they will be scanned under party supervision, delaying the count in the competitive 17th Congressional District until Wednesday. News 12's Nicholas Zifcak, reporting from the Board of Elections in White Plains, says counting at the BOE facility on the Saw Mill Parkway starts Wednesday at 11 a.m., and lohud reports County Executive Ken Jenkins says the ballots will be counted. Figures of 332 sites and 250,000 ballots circulating on X come from partisan and unverified accounts and are not confirmed by the county or the Board of Elections. lohud reports provisional paper ballots have been delivered to the Westchester Board of Elections, and The Rye Record reports the board says it will begin counting the emergency-bag ballots at 11 a.m. Wednesday. Update, 6 AM ET: ABC7NY (verified) reports the delayed Westchester ballots have been counted, with Conley and Bennett declared winners; Rep. Lawler had conceded NY-17 to Cait Conley before 11 p.m. Tuesday, per multiple posts. Figures of up to 332 sites and 250,000 ballots still trace to partisan outlets and are not confirmed by the county or the Board of Elections.
America.status: Delayed ballots reported counted (ABC7NY); stabilizing, moving to routine coverage
