FL Division of Emergency Management on EO 26-227 (verified)
CBS News, Port St. Lucie flooding (verified)

America.title: Flooding in northern Arizona
America.location: Sedona, Oak Creek and Coconino County, Arizona, USA
America.summary: Weekend storms flooded Oak Creek near Sedona and other parts of northern Arizona. The Arizona Emergency Information Network posted local assistance and road-hazard contacts for Coconino County, Flagstaff and Oak Creek. X News summaries report evacuations, road closures and a statewide emergency declaration, which were not confirmed in a linked official post.
America.status: Under investigation

America.title: Bexar County ballot scanner problems during early voting
America.summary: KSAT reported that election judges said some ballots were placed in scanners' emergency compartments during scanner problems at Bexar County early voting sites. The county declined an interview and said it could not provide a statement. The number of affected sites and how long the problems lasted have not been officially confirmed.
America.status: Early reports from local media; no official county statement

links.label: Post on X quoting KSAT reporting

Europe.title: Cyberattack enabled fraudulent transactions at French bank Crédit Mutuel Arkéa
Europe.summary: Crédit Mutuel Arkéa, a French cooperative banking group, has confirmed a cyberattack that allowed fraudulent operations, according to French media and posts relaying the bank's statement. On-chain investigator ZachXBT linked more than $133 million in suspicious exchange withdrawals to the bank, and French posts put the total above €100 million. The bank says the incident is under control and that clients will not bear losses; some transactions were reportedly suspended as a precaution.
Europe.status: Confirmed by the bank, per media reports; loss figure from an on-chain investigator, not the bank; attribution unknown

links.label: Louis Tellier, Blockstories (bank confirmation by email)

Europe.title: Fire at Tbilisi building housing opposition-leaning Formula TV; staff trapped
Europe.summary: A fire broke out at the business center in Tbilisi that houses Formula TV, one of Georgia's few remaining opposition-leaning broadcasters, and the channel went off air, Civil.ge reports. Part of the staff remained inside as firefighters arrived. A Georgian journalist posted that 22 people, including opposition leader Zurab Japaridze, were to be evacuated through windows and by crane because the stairs were too dangerous. The cause of the fire has not been reported.
Europe.status: Early reports; rescue under way; cause unknown; no casualty figures

Europe.title: Second wave of cyberattacks on supermarket refrigeration
Europe.location: Across Europe, including Belgium, Sweden, Germany, Romania and the UK
Europe.summary: Grocery stores in at least seven European countries saw refrigerator temperatures soar on Monday, and several confirmed a cyberattack similar to one in France three weeks ago. In Belgium, about 40 stores across Delhaize, Carrefour, Spa and other chains were hit, with about €100,000 of food thrown away. BBC reports a huge amount of food dumped in dozens of supermarkets across several countries, and Xinhua says the method matches the October attack in France, where hackers remotely raised temperatures. Security researcher Lukasz Olejnik now lists confirmed victims in Sweden, Belgium, Ireland, Luxembourg, Estonia, the Netherlands, Finland, Portugal, Germany and Italy, with Poland and Romania suspected. Sky News reports a top UK security official says the attacks have also affected the UK meat processing industry. Reuters now reports European supermarkets rushing to patch vulnerabilities, and Channel 4 News says GCHQ is alerting UK companies that could be at risk. AFP reports Germany, Romania and the UK joined the list of countries hit on Tuesday, and Sky News reports new warnings from the UK AI minister and the National Cyber Security Centre. The Hindu now puts the attack at 11 European countries, with store temperatures pushed as high as 50°C, and notes the attackers appear to seek disruption rather than ransom.
Europe.status: Confirmed by several companies and major outlets; UK meat processing impact reported by Sky News; attribution unknown

links.label: AFP: Germany, Romania and UK hit
Channel 4 News: GCHQ alerting UK firms

Europe.title: Cyberattack on French blood service contractor's cold storage
Europe.summary: Le Canard enchaîné reports that on the night of Nov 1–2 hackers attacked a contractor of the Établissement français du sang (EFS), France's blood service, and heated cold rooms holding blood samples, set to stay at minus 30 degrees, up to 110 degrees. FrenchBreaches names the contractor as Coolworld and says the incident was detected in time with no reported operational impact. It resembles the refrigeration attacks on European supermarkets. Update: The Hindu now also reports hackers breached systems to remotely heat EFS freezers holding donor blood samples and plasma. Update, 8 AM ET: the Daily Mail also reports blood-bank storage temperatures were raised by hackers following the supermarket freezer attacks.
Europe.status: Reported by Le Canard enchaîné; no EFS statement found on X this sweep; attribution unknown

Europe.title: Moldova suspects a state actor behind cyberattack
Europe.summary: Moldova's prime minister told Euronews the government suspects a state actor is behind a cyberattack. The Euronews post does not detail which systems were hit; unverified posts claim government databases and citizens' ID data were compromised.
Europe.status: Official statement reported by Euronews; scope and attribution under investigation

Europe.title: Bomb threats hit several European flights
Europe.location: Warsaw-Modlin and Warsaw Chopin airports, Poland; Murcia, Spain; Budapest, Hungary
Europe.summary: Bomb threats have now hit at least six passenger flights to Poland, Spain, Bulgaria and Italy. LOT flight LO286 from London diverted to Warsaw-Modlin, and Reuters says Modlin has since reopened. Two Ryanair flights to Rome Fiumicino, from Dublin and Lisbon, were escorted by Italian Air Force jets and searched after landing. Searches so far have found no explosives. The Daily Mail now reports the threats have spread, with multiple flights, including three from the UK, forced to make emergency landings.
Europe.status: No explosives found per reports so far; threats under investigation; no attribution

Europe.title: Violent cost-of-living and anti-government protests
Europe.summary: On Oct 31, masked rioters looted shops in Frankfurt, and German police fired water cannons at youths throwing Molotov cocktails. In Paris and elsewhere in France, police fired tear gas as hundreds of thousands marched against living costs and police violence. In Tirana, protesters threw Molotov cocktails and paving stones at police. Swiss paper Tages-Anzeiger says the riots also reached Switzerland over the weekend, with protests in Zurich. On Tuesday, French students marched through central Paris despite the authorities rejecting their route, Reuters reports, and DW says German officials are looking for those responsible for the Gen Z protest riots.
Europe.status: Confirmed by major outlets; further marches possible

Europe.title: Spyware alerts for German officials
Europe.summary: People who received the alerts were told to treat their phones as compromised. It is not yet known who is behind the attack or how many people were affected.
Europe.status: Under investigation

Europe.title: Poland deploys counterterrorism police near Kaliningrad
Europe.summary: Poland has deployed police counterterrorism units near the Kaliningrad border after intelligence warnings of possible sabotage in the coming days, the Kyiv Independent reports, citing Polish media.
Europe.status: Early reports; no incident reported

Europe.title: Latvia says drones violated its airspace
Europe.summary: Latvia believes one of two drones that violated its airspace was Russian and the other Ukrainian, Reuters reports.
Europe.status: Official assessment reported by Reuters

Europe.title: Germany arrests suspected organizer of Starlink ground station arson in Poland
Europe.location: Reutlingen district, Germany / Wola Krobowska, Poland
Europe.summary: German special police arrested a Turkish national on Nov 3 suspected of ordering the Sept 23 arson attack on a Starlink ground station south of Warsaw, according to a report citing Stuttgart prosecutors. Two alleged perpetrators were arrested in October. Polish prosecutors suspect Russian intelligence involvement, which German authorities have not confirmed.
Europe.status: Arrest reported; investigation ongoing

Russia.title: Russian drone strike sets Odesa's 7th Kilometer market on fire
Russia.summary: Russian drones struck the 7th Kilometer market near Odesa, one of Ukraine's largest wholesale markets, on Wednesday morning, starting a large fire seen on video. One account says the strike came during the working day while the market was busy. No official casualty figures were found in the posts reviewed.
Russia.status: Early reports with video; casualties unknown

Russia.title: Ukrainian drone strike sets Ozon logistics hub in Adygeysk on fire
Russia.summary: A drone attack overnight on November 4 set fire to online retailer Ozon's logistics centre in Adygeysk, damaging the building and partially collapsing its roof, Militarnyi reports. Ozon confirmed the attack and said staff were evacuated, with no casualties reported, and the head of Adygea also confirmed it. Videos posted by OSINT accounts show a large fire at the site.
Russia.status: Confirmed by the company and regional head, per reports; damage still being assessed

links.label: Open Source Intel: video of fire
Lew Anno: cites Ozon, Interfax, Kommersant

Russia.title: 310-drone overnight attack on Ukraine; Zhytomyr largely without power
Russia.location: Kyiv, Zhytomyr, Odesa and other regions, Ukraine
Russia.summary: Russia launched 310 drones overnight into November 4, according to Ukraine's Air Force as cited by journalist Michael Bociurkiw, targeting Kyiv, Dnipro, Poltava, Odesa, Ternopil and the Rivne and Kirovohrad regions. Hromadske Radio reports Zhytomyr remains largely without power after a strike, with electric transport suspended and water facilities on generators. Kyiv Post shows Kyiv in a blackout on generators, and Bociurkiw reports large parts of Odesa without power and Kyiv water only partly restored.
Russia.status: Ongoing; outages continuing

Russia.title: Russian bombing kills 33 at aid point in Komyshuvakha
Russia.summary: Zelenskyy said aerial bombs hit a school in Komyshuvakha, Zaporizhzhia Oblast, where people were receiving humanitarian aid, followed by more bombs on the shelter where people were taking cover. The Kyiv Independent reports at least 33 killed in the Nov 2 strikes, and Zelenskyy said on Nov 3 that more than 50 others may still be trapped under the rubble.
Russia.status: Toll rising; 33 killed per Kyiv Independent citing Zelenskyy; rescue continuing

Russia.title: Massive overnight Russian strike on Ukraine's power grid
Russia.location: Odesa, Cherkasy, Zhytomyr, Vinnytsia, Kharkiv, Dnipro, Chernivtsi, Chernihiv and Rivne regions, Ukraine
Russia.summary: President Zelenskyy says Russia launched 289 attack drones, 17 ballistic missiles and 59 cruise missiles overnight, mainly at power plants and substations across nine regions, and that emergency and unscheduled power outages are ongoing in many cities. He says a strike on a Kharkiv city clinical hospital injured 73 people and damaged its cardiology department. Anton Gerashchenko reports one person killed and at least 17 injured in Dnipro, and NOELreports lists the Ladyzhyn, Prydniprovska, Kryvorizka and Zmiivska thermal power plants as hit. The Kyiv Independent reports that Russian attacks across Ukraine killed 38 people and injured 158, and that a morning missile strike hit hospitals in Dnipro. The Kyiv Independent reports Kyiv now faces emergency power cuts and widespread water outages. The Kyiv Independent calls it Russia's biggest mass attack on Ukraine's energy infrastructure this year. Energy Minister Denys Shmyhal says three drones targeted a substation critical to the stable operation of the Khmelnytskyi Nuclear Power Plant during the attack, and Ukraine has informed the IAEA.
Russia.status: Official statement issued by Ukraine's president; air raid alerts continuing; no Ukrenergo damage assessment found this sweep; customer outage counts not confirmed

links.label: Kyiv Independent: Kyiv emergency power cuts
Liveuamap: Khmelnytskyi NPP substation targeted, per Shmyhal

Russia.title: New overnight Russian drone attack; eastern Kyiv power loss reported
Russia.summary: NOELreports, citing Ukraine's Air Force, says Russia launched 310 drones overnight into Nov. 4, including 81 jet-powered Shaheds, with 272 downed or suppressed and strikes recorded at 19 locations. OSINT account AMK Mapping says almost all of eastern Kyiv lost power overnight after jet-drone strikes on energy infrastructure, including the Kyivska 750 kV substation. The Kyiv outage and substation damage have not yet been confirmed by Ukrenergo, city officials or a major outlet. Update: UkraineWorld reports, citing Ukrenergo, that emergency power cuts in Kyiv cannot yet be lifted and scheduled outage timetables are not in force; drone debris caused fires in two districts.
Russia.status: Air Force figures relayed by an OSINT account; Kyiv blackout single-source, unconfirmed

links.label: AMK Mapping (OSINT): eastern Kyiv without power

Russia.title: Emergency alert apps in Ukraine and Russia hacked
Russia.summary: Ukraine and Russia both said their emergency alert apps had been hacked, sending false warnings about air raids and chemical and nuclear attacks. Russia said its app suffered a "massive cyberattack" on Monday, hours after Ukraine reported its own hack. In Ukraine the fake nuclear warning caused unease but not panic. Zelenskyy told PBS NewsHour that Ukraine targeted Russia's emergency alert systems in a retaliatory hack. Hackmanac reports the attacker exploited a flaw in the admin panel of the Russian Emergency Ministry app to push false alerts across 33 regions.
Russia.status: Officially confirmed by both governments; Zelenskyy says Ukraine's hack of Russian alerts was retaliation

Russia.title: Drone strike kills two at Russian-held Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant
Russia.location: Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant, Enerhodar, Ukraine
Russia.summary: The Russian-held Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant says a Ukrainian drone killed two people, including a station employee, Reuters reports. Ukraine's response and any IAEA comment weren't seen in this sweep.
Russia.status: Claim by the Russian-installed plant management, reported by Reuters; not independently confirmed

Russia.title: Ukrainian drone strike reported on Yaroslavl oil refinery
Russia.summary: The Kyiv Independent reports that Ukraine struck the Slavneft-YANOS oil refinery in Yaroslavl with drones overnight on Nov. 3, with residents reporting several fires at the facility, citing Ukrainian monitoring channels. OSINT accounts posted video of fires in the industrial zone, and the independent Russian outlet ASTRA reported explosions in the area. Russian officials had not confirmed damage or casualties at the time of this sweep. Kyiv Post reports the Slavneft-owned refinery caught fire after the drone attack.
Russia.status: Early reports; no official Russian statement yet

Russia.title: Ukrainian drone strike reported on Samara oil facility
Russia.summary: Ukrainian monitoring channels reported that Ukrainian drones struck the Samara Linear Production and Dispatch Station in Prosvet overnight. Kazakhstan reportedly suspended oil pumping through the Atyrau-Samara pipeline after the attack on the Samara hub, with its Energy Ministry cited via TASS.
Russia.status: Strike reported by Ukrainian channels; Kazakh halt reported via TASS and market wires, not yet seen from major Western outlets

links.label: Post citing TASS on Kazakh halt (unverified account)

Russia.title: Large Ukrainian drone raid toward western Russia under way tonight
Russia.summary: OSINTtechnical reports a Ukrainian attack drone raid into western Russia is under way tonight, with local channels reporting jet-powered drones in the mix and several hundred drones headed toward Russian targets. It follows five straight nights of hits on Russian oil installations. Separately, Eyewitness News reports Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said Tuesday that air defenses downed nearly 500 drones headed toward the capital; it isn't clear whether that figure covers tonight's raid.
Russia.status: OSINT reports of a large raid; Moscow mayor's drone-downing claim reported by EWN; no independent damage reports yet

links.label: Eyewitness News: Sobyanin says nearly 500 drones downed

Russia.title: Widespread blackout across Russian-occupied Crimea
Russia.summary: Accounts on both sides report a widespread power outage across Crimea on Nov. 3–4, with video of Simferopol in darkness. ConflictRadarME quotes Oleg Kryuchkov, an adviser to the Russian-installed Crimean head, saying an incident on external grid infrastructure cut the main supply. A pro-Russian WarGonzo account reports rolling cuts, water pumping problems and emergency mobile roaming, and Beefeater, citing Crimea.Realities, reports fuel shortages. The cause is not established.
Russia.status: Early reports from partisan and OSINT accounts; no major-outlet confirmation yet

Middle East.title: Houthi missile strike on Lahj health center kills five
Middle East.summary: A ballistic missile attributed to the Houthis hit the Al-Saqiya health center in Lahj, killing five people and injuring 15, including medical staff, according to Yemen's government-aligned forces and local outlets. UNICEF, which supports the center, said the attack was deeply concerning, and the British ambassador to Yemen condemned it. Separately, South24 cites a military source saying a Houthi missile hit a detention site in Lahj early Wednesday, killing two.
Middle East.status: Casualty toll from Yemeni government side; UN agency and UK ambassador statements reported; second strike single-source

Middle East.title: IRGC claims it shot down a US MQ-9 Reaper over the Strait of Hormuz
Middle East.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards say they shot down a US MQ-9 Reaper drone over the Strait of Hormuz early Wednesday and released video they say shows the hit. The claim is circulating through OSINT and aggregator accounts. No US military confirmation was found on X this sweep.
Middle East.status: Unconfirmed IRGC claim; no CENTCOM statement found

Middle East.title: Missile strike on recruit training camp in Yemen's Al Dhale
Middle East.location: Al-Alalah camp, Qa'tabah district, Al Dhale, Yemen
Middle East.summary: Yemeni outlets report a ballistic missile strike attributed to the Houthis hit the Al-Alalah training camp for new recruits in Qa'tabah district on Wednesday morning. An unnamed medical source puts the provisional toll at 7 killed and 50 wounded. Tolls vary across posts and there is no official confirmation yet.
Middle East.status: Early reports; multiple local outlets; toll provisional

Middle East.title: US strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island
Middle East.location: Qeshm Island, Strait of Hormuz, Iran
Middle East.summary: A US official told Reuters that the US carried out strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz late Monday, Nov. 2. The Economic Times, citing The Wall Street Journal, says it is the latest in a series of limited, unpublicized US strikes in recent weeks. Iran's state news agency IRNA earlier reported five explosions on the island. Officials quoted in media describe the strike as a defensive response to Iranian surface-to-air fire on a US aircraft; CENTCOM has not issued a statement. An Israeli military spokesperson says Israel was not involved. On Nov 3, President Trump said the US carried out a "minor attack" in Iran overnight, claiming Iranian ships and planes were destroyed and insisting it was not a war, per Al Jazeera. Iran's security chief said the Strait of Hormuz would reopen only if the US met Iran's seven conditions. Later on Nov 3, Reuters, citing a Financial Times interview, reported Trump said the US has no immediate plan to strike Iran again.
Middle East.status: US strikes acknowledged by President Trump; damage and casualty claims not independently confirmed; no CENTCOM statement found

links.label: Reuters: no immediate plan to strike Iran, per FT (verified)
Al Jazeera English: Israel says not involved (verified)

Middle East.title: Indian cargo dhow struck off Oman; one sailor killed
Middle East.summary: India's shipping minister says the Indian vessel MSV AL JUSUFI, carrying 14 Indian seafarers, was struck by an unidentified aerial object near the Omani coast on Nov. 2. One crew member was killed and 13 were rescued by the Omani Coast Guard. India's foreign ministry condemned the attack and called continuing attacks on shipping in the region deeply concerning.
Middle East.status: Official statement issued; attacker not identified

Middle East.title: Tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz
Middle East.summary: UKMTO says a tanker's security officer reported the ship was struck by two unknown projectiles in its engine room around 2 PM ET Tuesday, about 14 nautical miles northeast of Lima, Oman, with no casualties or environmental impact reported. OSINTdefender notes it is at least the third vessel reportedly hit in that area in under two weeks. Iran's IRGC Navy earlier claimed three oil tankers exploded after hitting naval mines while transiting without Iranian permission, and a navigational warning says the tug Selat Storm has sunk west of Jazirat Um al Ghanam. Update: Reuters reports the IRGC now says four tankers are ablaze after hitting mines near the Strait of Hormuz, and Iran International says the IRGC also claims two other vessels were stopped and a US MQ-9 drone shot down. Those claims could not be independently verified. Iranian state outlet IranPress separately repeats the UKMTO report of the projectile strike near Lima, Oman.
Middle East.status: UKMTO-reported strike near Lima, Oman (no casualties); IRGC claims of four tankers ablaze, two vessels stopped and a downed MQ-9 are unverified

links.label: Reuters: IRGC says four tankers ablaze (verified)
Iran International English: IRGC claims, not independently verified
Al Jazeera English on new IRGC claim (verified)

Middle East.title: Internet outages reported in Tehran
Middle East.location: Tehran and other parts of Iran
Middle East.summary: Iran International, citing Iranian media, reports internet outages on the MCI and Telecommunications Company of Iran networks in parts of Tehran and severe slowdowns elsewhere. Access to the global internet was reportedly cut for about 10 minutes before being restored.
Middle East.status: Early reports via Iranian media; no NetBlocks or official confirmation found this sweep

Middle East.title: Gunfire reported in Bandar Abbas and Sirik
Middle East.location: Bandar Abbas and Sirik, Hormozgan, Iran
Middle East.summary: The IRGC-affiliated Tasnim news agency reported sounds of gunfire in Bandar Abbas and Sirik in southern Iran, based on residents' accounts, per Iran International. Tasnim said no official source had confirmed the reports.
Middle East.status: Unconfirmed; residents' accounts only

Middle East.title: Syria says it foiled Hezbollah plot to attack Homs oil refinery
Middle East.summary: Reuters reports Syria says it foiled a Hezbollah plot to attack the Homs oil refinery. No attack took place.
Middle East.status: Official claim reported by Reuters; details and Hezbollah response not seen

Middle East.title: Unconfirmed report of explosion at British Embassy in Baghdad
Middle East.summary: Iran's Tasnim News Agency reported explosions heard inside the British Embassy in Baghdad. Other accounts describe a roadside device hitting a diplomatic vehicle instead. No official confirmation, casualties or damage details have been seen.
Middle East.status: Single-source and unconfirmed

Middle East.title: Houthis claim drone strikes on Saudi Arabia's Dammam airport
Middle East.summary: Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree claimed drone attacks over the past 48 hours on Dammam airport, which he said disrupted air traffic, and on military targets in Jizan. The Saudi-led coalition said air defenses intercepted two drones over the Riyadh region, with no damage or casualties disclosed. The Houthi claims about Dammam have not been independently confirmed.
Middle East.status: Unconfirmed claims; coalition statement on Riyadh interceptions

Middle East.title: Unexplained explosion in Iraq's Diyala province
Middle East.summary: Faytuks Network reports an explosion on the outskirts of Diyala that was reportedly heard in neighboring Salah al-Din, with locals describing intense military aircraft activity. Security officials told Iraqi Sabereen News the cause and nature of the blast are unknown.
Middle East.status: Early reports; cause unknown; no official statement

Middle East.title: Israeli air strike kills police officers near Khan Younis
Middle East.summary: Gaza's interior ministry says an Israeli air strike killed and wounded several police officers near Khan Younis. The number of casualties wasn't given.
Middle East.status: Single-sided claim (Gaza interior ministry) reported by Al Jazeera; no Israeli military comment found this sweep

Middle East.title: Drones strike Iranian Kurdish group Komala's HQ near Erbil
Middle East.location: Alana Valley, northeast of Erbil, Iraqi Kurdistan
Middle East.summary: Komala says two explosive drones hit its headquarters on Nov 4, causing property damage and no casualties, and blames Iran's IRGC. Iranian responsibility is the group's allegation only.
Middle East.status: Single-source roundup citing Rudaw

Africa.title: Johannesburg power outages on local election day
Africa.summary: City Power reported several faults on the morning of South Africa's local government elections, including an outage at Boothill Switching Station affecting Wilgeheuwel, Honeydew and nearby areas, and one at Mayfair Substation affecting Amalgam. Teams were on site investigating; some other outages, such as Orchards and Ennerdale, were fully or mostly restored. No impact on specific voting stations was reported in the posts reviewed.
Africa.status: Official statements issued by City Power; repairs ongoing

Africa.title: Dynamite blast at Ghana–Burkina Faso border kills immigration officer; curfew imposed
Africa.location: Hamile, Lambussie District, Upper West Region, Ghana
Africa.summary: A suspected load of dynamite on a tricycle exploded at Hamile on the Burkina Faso border early Tuesday, killing an immigration officer, according to several Ghanaian outlets. The Interior Ministry imposed a 6 PM to 5 AM curfew on Hamile and banned arms and ammunition. The district's chief executive said youths massed against immigration officers after the blast. Citi FM reports Muntaka urged chiefs and elders to calm agitated youth, and that the Ghana Immigration Service cautioned the public against circulating unverified reports. Update: the Ghanaian Times now reports at least three people dead and others critically injured in the suspected dynamite explosion in Hamile; earlier reports cited one immigration officer killed. The toll has not been confirmed in an official post reviewed. Update: Ghanaian Times reports at least three dead and others critically injured; an 11-hour daily curfew has been imposed in Hamile.
Africa.status: Official curfew issued; cause and full toll still being reported

links.label: Ghanaian Times: at least three dead
Citi FM: calls to calm youth
Citi FM: GIS warns on unverified reports

Africa.title: Mapleton power restored, but water outages continue in Gauteng-area municipalities
Africa.location: Ekurhuleni, Tshwane (Pretoria), Lesedi, Govan Mbeki, Victor Khanye and Thembisile Hani municipalities, South Africa
Africa.summary: The City of Ekurhuleni says power has been restored at the Mapleton substation that feeds Rand Water's Mapleton Pumping Station in Boksburg, after a failure that cut water to six municipalities including the Ekurhuleni and Tshwane metros. Parts of Thembisa and Tsakane still have low pressure or no water while reservoirs refill, and the city has sent water tankers. eNCA says Ekurhuleni's mayor expects the system to be fully restored overnight.
Africa.status: Power restored per the City of Ekurhuleni; water supply recovering; full restoration expected overnight

Africa.title: Bandits ambush police on Sokoto–Gusau highway
Africa.summary: Suspected bandits ambushed police officers traveling from Sokoto to Zamfara State for special duty, killing at least five, according to New Telegraph. Local outlets report some officers were abducted and say police confirmed the attack.
Africa.status: Confirmed by police, per local reports

Africa.title: Explosion at Metafrique Steel plant in Douala
Africa.summary: An explosion at the Metafrique Steel plant killed at least four people and severely burned 16, the regional governor said. The cause is under investigation.
Africa.status: Official toll from regional governor; cause under investigation

Africa.title: Johannesburg water crisis
Africa.summary: Residents and civic activists planned a protest outside Johannesburg Water's head office, and the Joburg Crisis Alliance is threatening legal action against the city over unreliable water supply. The mayor says intensified technical work is beginning to improve supply. On Nov 3, the mayor said water storage across Johannesburg's system has improved to more than 41 percent, up from 37 percent over the weekend, per SABC News.
Africa.status: Improving per the mayor

Africa.title: MK Party organiser shot dead before KZN local elections
Africa.summary: MK Party regional organiser Lastborn Shazi was shot dead at his home in Umzumbe during preparations for South Africa's local government elections. KZN police spokesperson Col. Robert Netshiunda appealed for calm and asked the public to give police space to investigate the murder.
Africa.status: Police investigating; no arrests reported

Africa.title: At least eight killed in attack in Nigeria's Zamfara state
Africa.summary: CGTN Africa's bulletin reports at least eight people killed in an attack in Zamfara state. No details on attackers or location were given in the post.
Africa.status: Single-source report

Africa.title: Lagos Island residents protest days-long power outages
Africa.summary: Residents of Lagos Island took to the streets to protest a prolonged lack of electricity in their communities, according to Silverbird Television.
Africa.status: Early reports; single outlet

Africa.title: Suspected RSF drone strike kills seven in South Kordofan
Africa.summary: CGTN Africa reports seven people killed in a suspected RSF drone strike in South Kordofan. Details on the target were not given.
Africa.status: Single outlet

Africa.title: Al-Shabab attack on army position near Xarardheere
Africa.summary: A Somali news account reports a heavy Al-Shabab attack early Wednesday on a federal military position at Faax. Casualties among government forces are reported but unconfirmed, and it is unclear whether the position was overrun.
Africa.status: Early, single-source report

South America.title: Explosive thrown at Media Canoa toll plaza in Valle del Cauca
South America.summary: Men on a motorcycle threw an explosive at the Media Canoa toll on the Cali–Buga road around 3:45 a.m. Wednesday, damaging two lanes, according to Revista Semana, El País Cali and BLU Radio, citing police. No injuries were reported. Police are seeking those responsible, and no group has claimed it.
South America.status: Reported by several established Colombian outlets citing police; no injuries

South America.title: Protests over power cuts in several Venezuelan cities
South America.location: Carabobo, Lara, Cojedes and Aragua states, Venezuela
South America.summary: Residents protested overnight over long power cuts in Los Guayos (Carabobo), Barquisimeto (Lara), Tinaco (Cojedes) and Maracay, according to local journalists and residents' posts, with some areas reportedly without power for up to 24 hours. No injuries or arrests were reported in the posts reviewed, and no statement from the electricity company Corpoelec was found.
South America.status: Early reports from local accounts; no established-outlet confirmation yet

South America.title: Truck bomb near military base in Planadas, Colombia
South America.summary: A truck loaded with explosives detonated near a military base in Planadas, Tolima, killing four civilians, including a two-month-old girl, an official said. The blast heavily damaged a hospital, a school and several homes, and reports citing Colombia's Defense Ministry put the injured at 17. Colombian authorities have named two FARC dissident commanders under alias Iván Mordisco as responsible, NTN24 reports, and residents held a candlelight vigil Tuesday evening. Revista Semana reports Planadas's mayor has asked for a speedy investigation into the attack.
South America.status: Confirmed by officials and major outlets; attributed by authorities to FARC dissidents

links.label: Revista Semana: mayor seeks swift investigation
NTN24 (verified): authorities name two dissident commanders
Diario El Salvador citing Colombia's Defense Ministry

South America.title: Clashes in Asunción as Ueno Bank depositors protest central bank takeover
South America.summary: Última Hora reports Ueno Bank depositors and employees clashed with National Police on Tuesday night in downtown Asunción while protesting the central bank's resolution of the digital lender, with riot police blocking them from reaching the National Congress area. NPY carried live coverage of the protests. Reuters reports Paraguay's central bank chief resigned at the president's request as the crisis deepened.
South America.status: Ongoing; reported by two Paraguayan outlets, with Reuters on the banking crisis; no injury or arrest figures seen

links.label: Última Hora: riot police block route to Congress

South America.title: Second police officer dies after motorbike bomb in Algeciras, Huila
South America.summary: Colombia's National Police announced the death of a patrolman gravely wounded in Sunday's terrorist attack in Algeciras, Huila. Noticias Caracol reports he is the second police officer to die from the motorbike bomb.
South America.status: Official statement issued

South America.title: Drone attack kills two soldiers in Colombia's Chocó
South America.summary: DW Español reports two soldiers were killed and five wounded in a drone attack in a rural area of Chocó. It is the second explosives attack in Colombia in under 24 hours, after the Planadas truck bomb. Noticias RNN also reports a drone attack killing two soldiers and wounding five. Commentator Manuel Pedrero places a drone attack on the El Trapiche military post in Ocaña, Norte de Santander, and says authorities blamed the ELN; it is unclear whether that is the same attack, so the location is unresolved.
South America.status: Reported by an established outlet; no claim of responsibility seen

South America.title: Security breach halts Brazil's Mercado Bitcoin exchange
South America.summary: Mercado Bitcoin, one of Brazil's largest crypto exchanges, said it identified and contained a security incident in one of its systems overnight and suspended deposits and withdrawals as a precaution. In a later update it put the assets involved at about US$38 million and said about US$11 million had been frozen with partners including Tether and Circle. The exchange says customers will not lose assets and no data was leaked; services remained suspended with no restart time given.
South America.status: Official statement issued; services suspended

South America.title: Magnitude 5.6 earthquake in Tolima, Colombia
South America.summary: The Colombian Geological Service says a magnitude 5.6 earthquake struck at 4:13 a.m. local time on Nov 3 with its epicenter near Chaparral, Tolima, at a shallow depth of about 19 km. El Tiempo, citing the national disaster agency, says one person was injured, and Noticias Caracol reports a woman in Chaparral was hurt when a wall fell on her. El Tiempo also reports serious damage to homes in Chaparral based on social media video.
South America.status: Official statement issued by the Colombian Geological Service; damage assessment ongoing

South America.title: Protesters block Morón–Coro highway over power failures
South America.summary: Caraota Digital reports residents blocked the Morón–Coro highway in another protest over electrical failures, demanding answers from authorities.
South America.status: Single-source local report

South America.title: Colombian police say they foiled a bomb attack on a Pan-American Highway toll
South America.location: Nariño, Colombia, near the Ecuador border
South America.summary: UHN Plus reports that Colombia's president said police foiled an attack on a toll station on the Pan-American Highway in Nariño and found 117 kilos of explosives.
South America.status: Single source this sweep; no post from Colombian police or the presidency found on X

South America.title: Explosion and fire at Zulia substation reported to cut power
South America.location: Federación substation, Ciudad Ojeda, Zulia, Venezuela
South America.summary: An activist account reports a loud explosion followed by a fire at the Federación electrical substation in Ciudad Ojeda, leaving parts of Zulia without power. Scale and cause aren't known.
South America.status: Early reports; single non-official source; no statement from Corpoelec found

South America.title: Drone and rifle attack on police station in Chimichagua, Cesar
South America.summary: El Tiempo reports a drone and rifle attack on the police station in Chimichagua, Cesar, left no one injured. Noticias Caracol earlier reported a drone attack against police in Cesar department.
South America.status: Reported by two established outlets; no injuries reported

South America.title: US reportedly helped Venezuela in deadly strike on ELN in Apure
South America.summary: Infobae, carrying a New York Times report, says US officials say the US helped Venezuela carry out a lethal drone strike on an ELN guerrilla base in Apure. Casualty figures were not in the post.
South America.status: Reported by major outlet citing officials

threats.title: GitHub degraded: pull requests, git operations and Actions
threats.summary: GitHub's status page reported elevated errors on pull requests, git operations, issues and Actions starting around 9:49 UTC Wednesday. No sign of a cyberattack; it is described as a partial outage under investigation.
threats.status: Under investigation by GitHub

threats.title: Unverified claim of Diners Club Ecuador database leak
threats.summary: A threat actor on a dark web forum claims to have stolen and leaked the full database of card issuer Diners Club Ecuador, according to Dark Web Intelligence. The contents have not been verified and the company has not confirmed an incident.
threats.status: Unverified threat-actor claim

threats.title: Suspected blast damages railway track near India–Pakistan border
threats.summary: A suspected explosion around 9:45 p.m. local time Tuesday damaged two concrete supports under the Anupgarh–Suratgarh railway line near village 50 GB in Sri Ganganagar district, close to the Pakistan border. Free Press Journal reports two trains were cancelled, and First India reports the state anti-terror squad (ATS) is involved. No casualties are reported, and the cause is under investigation; claims of sabotage from OSINT and partisan accounts are unconfirmed.
threats.status: Under investigation; no casualties reported; train services disrupted

threats.title: North Korea fires multiple missiles toward Sea of Japan
threats.summary: South Korea's military says North Korea fired several missiles into the Sea of Japan, its fourth weapons launch in a month, according to Reuters and Al Jazeera English. No damage or casualties have been reported.
threats.status: Reported by Seoul via major outlets; missile type and range not yet given

threats.title: Unsupported claim of Iranian hypersonic strike on Israeli bases
threats.summary: Low-follower and partisan accounts are posting that Iran launched a massive hypersonic missile attack on several Israeli military bases and killed senior officials. No established outlet, IDF or Home Front Command post confirming a new barrage was found in this sweep, so it is not being elevated.
threats.status: Unconfirmed; no credible corroboration

threats.title: GitBook security incident; services restored
threats.summary: GitBook said it was addressing a security incident that took some services offline, then said its app, API and published docs were available again, with some services possibly still degraded.
threats.status: Official statements issued by GitBook; largely restored

threats.title: UK warns of AI-powered attack on critical infrastructure
threats.summary: The UK's National Cyber Security Centre said Britain should be prepared for an AI-powered cyberattack on its critical national infrastructure within two years, and named China as likely the best equipped, per Reuters.
threats.status: Official assessment; no specific incident

threats.title: Record $6.3bn Binance hack
threats.summary: More than $6 billion in crypto assets were stolen from Binance in a hack the FBI blamed on North Korea, according to AFP. North Korea denies responsibility. Reuters reports the attackers used a fake job interview to compromise a computer before the theft.
threats.status: Under investigation

threats.title: Cyberattack at Spandana Sphoorty Financial
threats.summary: India's Spandana Sphoorty Financial reported a cyberattack involving its bank account.
threats.status: Company-reported

threats.title: Unsupported 'coordinated attack' claims
threats.summary: Posts linking the DC outage, the EU fridge attacks and other outages as one coordinated event have no evidence. Treat them as separate incidents.
threats.status: Unverified

threats.title: Dropped as stabilized or below the bar
threats.summary: Removed this sweep: the clashes at a facility near Kyiv (stabilized; police say the detention allegations were false). Earlier removals: the DC Foggy Bottom outage, the Richmond pump station outage, the San Diego registrar evacuation (cleared), the Mississauga police incident, the Hebron operation, the Florida Learjet crash, and the Fairfield and Moss Landing shootings. A seven-minute pause for a school safety drill at a Gwinnett County, GA polling place, with a requested seven-minute extension, was below the bar. The Oct. 28 Urda, Spain high-speed train collision is past the acute phase; Spain's transport minister said Tuesday he will resign over it (Reuters).

threats.title: Viral 'another Maricopa vote center closed' claim is unsourced
threats.summary: Posts claim a second, 'Republican-leaning' Maricopa County vote center in Mesa closed for a power outage, some calling for the election to be stopped. Maricopa County Elections' own posts show only the Laveen Elementary School District Office closure for a power outage early Tuesday, and no official source confirms a second closure.
threats.status: Unconfirmed; not elevated

threats.title: Low-priority log
threats.summary: Fraud and 'rigged' framing of the Westchester scanner failure, the Fulton County rescan and the Maricopa Laveen outage has no official support. Unverified posts claim the refrigeration attacks spread to 13 European countries and to US military installations. A 'Worldwide Alert' roundup from the Paul Gold Eagle account mixes real events with unsupported claims. A Florida 'state beach shooting' post from a low-credibility account appears to confuse the Moss Landing, California shooting and has no corroboration. Claims of an official 90-day blackout warning have no official source. Earlier unsupported claims (Jacksonville blackout, a successful Iranian strike on a US base in Kuwait, Russia hitting six power plants) still have no corroboration. Posts claiming widespread Pennsylvania scanner failures got a reply from the Pennsylvania Department of State saying scanner jams don't stop ballots from being counted and that it has no reports of widespread scanner issues. Viral 'Iran nuclear survival guide' and 'massive Iran internet blackout' posts come from low-credibility accounts; see the sourced internet-outage item instead. 7:30 PM sweep: viral video of multi-hour lines in Columbus, OH is circulating as Election Day footage, but replies identify it as past early-voting footage from the Franklin County Board of Elections site, so it was not logged. Unverified claims that Newaygo County, MI ran out of ballots and that Wayne County polls lost power just before closing found no official or verified-outlet support. Partisan 'cheating' framing around the Gibraltar threat was ignored. 8 PM sweep: a viral post claiming Wayne County polling places lost power remains unsupported beyond the single Canton Township report logged above; claims of a Mesa, AZ vote-center power closure 'per the Recorder's Office' still have no official source. New this sweep: a small account claims a 'BulkaHackers' arrest in Kosovo with no corroboration; posts framing Wayne County results as delayed countywide by fraud have no official support; posts claiming an Iranian missile barrage on Israel are contradicted in replies and by the lack of any official or major-outlet report; and PaulGoldEagle-style posts claiming more Ohio threats remain unsupported. New tonight: an unverified viral post claims a San Diego library ballot drop box overflowed and ballots were mishandled; the San Diego County Registrar has not addressed it on X, and it is not confirmed. A King County, WA 'voter fraud' video claim comes from a low-credibility account with no official support. Claims of a 'major power outage' on Colorado's Front Range are contradictory and have no utility or official source. Claims that Iran launched a massive hypersonic missile attack on Israeli bases come from low-credibility accounts and are not reported by the IDF or major outlets. 2:00 AM sweep: a new Paul Gold Eagle roundup lists Election Day voting disruptions across several states and frames them as deliberate interference without official confirmation; it is not logged as an alert.
threats.status: Unverified; not elevated

America.title: Shooting in Spokane County, WA kills two civilians; two deputies critically injured
America.summary: Officials announced Tuesday night that two civilians were killed and two Spokane County sheriff's deputies were critically injured in a shooting Tuesday afternoon. The suspect is dead. The incident is over and there is no indication of a wider threat; motive and details have not been released in the posts reviewed.
America.status: Confirmed by officials, per multiple reports; incident over

America.title: Ballot scanners failing across Westchester County polling places
America.summary: Westchester County says its Board of Elections is aware of an issue with the paper ballots that is stopping voting machines from accepting them at polling locations throughout the county. Voters are still filling out paper ballots, which poll workers are placing in secure emergency bags to be counted later. New York Attorney General Letitia James says her office is monitoring and in touch with state and local election boards, and NBC News and lohud report machines down at multiple sites, including White Plains. Al Jazeera English also reports the scanner failures and says ballots are being collected in emergency orange bags to be counted later. Rep. Lawler and others say the bags will be police-escorted to the Board of Elections after polls close at 9 p.m., New York's normal closing time. Update, unconfirmed: an unverified account posts that Westchester County Police will take about 90,000 sealed, unscanned ballots to the Board of Elections, to be unsealed tomorrow in front of watchers before counting. No official Westchester or Board of Elections post confirming that figure or timeline was found. Update: the RNC's election-integrity account says the unscanned ballots will go under police custody to the Board of Elections for central counting with watchers present, and that counting will begin no later than 11 a.m. Wednesday. That timing comes from a partisan account and hasn't been posted by the county or the Board of Elections on X. Update, midnight ET: a judge issued emergency rules for counting the unscanned ballots, Spectrum News NY1's Gloria Pazmino reports, and Examiner Media says Republicans and Democrats agreed to seek court approval for a supervised process to secure and count them. Deccan Chronicle, carrying a wire report, says the judge let officials move thousands of paper ballots to a secure county warehouse under police escort, where they will be scanned under party supervision, delaying the count in the competitive 17th Congressional District until Wednesday. News 12's Nicholas Zifcak, reporting from the Board of Elections in White Plains, says counting at the BOE facility on the Saw Mill Parkway starts Wednesday at 11 a.m., and lohud reports County Executive Ken Jenkins says the ballots will be counted. Figures of 332 sites and 250,000 ballots circulating on X come from partisan and unverified accounts and are not confirmed by the county or the Board of Elections. lohud reports provisional paper ballots have been delivered to the Westchester Board of Elections, and The Rye Record reports the board says it will begin counting the emergency-bag ballots at 11 a.m. Wednesday. Update, 6 AM ET: ABC7NY (verified) reports the delayed Westchester ballots have been counted, with Conley and Bennett declared winners; Rep. Lawler had conceded NY-17 to Cait Conley before 11 p.m. Tuesday, per multiple posts. Figures of up to 332 sites and 250,000 ballots still trace to partisan outlets and are not confirmed by the county or the Board of Elections.
America.status: Delayed ballots reported counted (ABC7NY); stabilizing, moving to routine coverage

America.title: DDoS attack briefly knocked Colorado's election results website offline
America.summary: The Denver Post reports a distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) bot attack hit the vendor behind the Colorado Secretary of State's public-facing election webpage Tuesday night, temporarily taking the site offline. Denver Post reporter Seth Klamann says the same vendor has been hit in other states and that the issue should now be resolved. The attack affected the public results display, and no report says voting or vote counting was affected.
America.status: Reported by The Denver Post; reportedly resolved; no Secretary of State post seen on X yet; other affected states not named

America.title: Some Dearborn precincts ran out of ballots; mayor says restock coming
America.summary: Detroit Free Press reporter Niraj Warikoo reports Dearborn Mayor Abdullah Hammoud said some precincts ran out of ballots but would be restocked soon, and urged voters to stay in line. Al Jazeera English also reports ballot shortages at several Dearborn polling stations and the mayor's appeal not to leave lines.
America.status: Mayor's statement reported by two outlets; restock under way; no clerk statement seen on X

links.label: Niraj Warikoo, Detroit Free Press reporter

America.title: Several Newaygo County, MI jurisdictions ran out of ballots
America.summary: FOX 17 in West Michigan reports the Newaygo County clerk's office confirmed that multiple jurisdictions in the county ran out of ballots on Election Day. Lower-credibility accounts add that more ballots were brought in and that voters in line by 8 p.m. could still vote, but that detail isn't confirmed by an official or verified outlet on X.
America.status: Clerk's office confirmation reported by one local outlet

America.title: Delayed opening and brief power outage at some Harris County polling sites
America.summary: KPRC 2 reports a delayed opening, a brief power outage and flickering lights at several Harris County polling sites, but says election workers reported voting continued smoothly afterward.
America.status: Resolved per KPRC 2; single outlet

America.title: Bomb threat at Gibraltar Carlson High School polling place; voting resumed
America.location: Gibraltar / Brownstown Township, Wayne County, MI
America.summary: WXYZ Detroit, citing the Brownstown Township Police Department, reports a bomb threat was called in Tuesday evening to Gibraltar Carlson High School, the polling location for precincts 8 and 11. WXYZ says voting moved outside while police swept the building. NewsForce (verified) reports voters were evacuated, and The Detroit News reports the threat prompted an evacuation of the polling place. A low-follower news aggregator quotes WXYZ as saying a Secretary of State spokesperson called the threat unfounded and the building was cleared, and other low-follower accounts cite a headline saying police have identified a suspect. Neither point has been confirmed by police or a verified outlet on X. The Detroit Free Press (verified) now reports police evacuated Carlson High School after the threat was called in, and The Detroit News (verified) reports, citing another outlet, that a suspect has been identified. Update: WDIV Local 4 reports voting resumed at Carlson High School, which serves Brownstown Township Precincts 8 and 11, according to Township Clerk Maureen Brinker, and that Gibraltar Police Chief Bruce Bullard said a suspect has been identified.
America.status: Voting resumed per the Brownstown Township clerk (via WDIV); suspect identified per the Gibraltar police chief (via WDIV); threat reported as not credible

America.title: Counting backlog in Indiana's most populous county could delay results
America.summary: WNDU reports a backlog in counting ballots in Indiana's most populous county that could delay some election results. No details on the cause or the number of ballots were in the post, and no post from the Marion County Election Board was found this sweep.
America.status: Single established local outlet; no official statement found on X

America.title: Printing error on 32,000 Washoe County mail ballot envelopes
America.summary: About 32,000 mail ballot return envelopes in Washoe County were printed with the word "FALSE" in a field meant to be blank, per posts citing CNN. Officials are quoted as saying the vendor error does not invalidate ballots or affect anyone's right to vote. Reported before Election Day and resurfacing tonight.
America.status: Reported via secondhand accounts citing CNN and officials; no county post found on X this sweep

America.title: User reports Pinellas County election-night results site crashed
America.summary: One account posted that Pinellas County's election-night reporting site crashed and tagged the county elections office. There's no confirmation from the Supervisor of Elections or local media.
America.status: Unverified; single non-official source

America.title: Federalsburg, MD results stand after voting machine error
America.summary: A local Eastern Shore outlet reports the town released its municipal election results and that they will stand after a voting machine error. The nature of the error wasn't detailed in the post.
America.status: Resolved per local media; single source

America.title: Power outage at a Canton Township polling site; voting continued
America.summary: The RNC's election-integrity account says it is in contact with DTE Energy about a power outage in Canton Township and that voting was ongoing. No DTE, county clerk, Secretary of State or verified local outlet post confirming the outage or its effect on voting turned up in this sweep. Viral posts describing a broad 'Wayne County power outage' at polling places are not supported by any official source.
America.status: Single partisan-organization source; no official confirmation; voting reported ongoing

America.title: NAACP seeks extended hours at a Prince George's County polling place
America.summary: The NAACP says it is moving to request extended hours at a Prince George's County polling location after problems earlier in the day stopped ballots from being cast. The post does not name the site. Election officials' confirmation of the problem or of any extension was not found in this sweep.
America.status: Single advocacy-group source; extension request not confirmed by officials

America.title: Fire extends voting hours at Kingston, PA polling place
America.location: Hoyt Library, Kingston, Luzerne County, PA
America.summary: WNEP reports that a fire led to voting hours being extended until 9 p.m. at the Hoyt Library polling place in Kingston. No details on the fire's cause or injuries were given.
America.status: Early report from a single local outlet; no county election office post found

America.title: Leavenworth County, KS polling place ran out of ballots in the morning
America.location: Linwood Community Building, Leavenworth County, KS
America.summary: The Kansas City Star reports a Leavenworth County polling place ran out of ballots early Tuesday. Posts citing KSHB 41 say a clerical error left the Linwood site with about 100 House District 38 ballots instead of about 1,000 around 8 a.m., and the shortage was resolved by about 10 a.m. Viral posts claiming 100,000 ballots were needed are wrong.
America.status: Resolved per local media

America.title: Conflicting reports on machines at Berkeley County, SC precinct
America.location: Howe Hall precinct, Berkeley County, SC
America.summary: SC state Rep. JA Moore posted that voting machines were down at the Howe Hall precinct and voters were being told to cast provisional ballots. The SC State Election Commission replied that Berkeley County officials said they were not aware of any machine issues or problems with voters casting ballots.
America.status: Disputed; official election commission says no known issue

America.title: Scattered polling problems delay closing times in several states
America.summary: Al Jazeera English reports a handful of polling locations across the US had technical issues with how ballots are cast, causing officials to delay poll closing times in some places. This matches the individual extensions already logged in North Carolina, Pennsylvania, Ohio and New York.
America.status: Reported by an established outlet; no count of affected sites

America.title: Chicago polling places run out of ballots; long lines
America.summary: Block Club Chicago reports voters spent hours in line as polling places across the city ran out of ballots. Earlier, an AP reporter said a Logan Square polling place ran out of ballots twice, with poll workers saying they received about 50 of the ballots needed for one precinct that morning. Aggregator posts claim six more sites ran short and that extra ballots were printed, but no Chicago Board of Elections statement was found on X this sweep.
America.status: Reported by Block Club Chicago and an on-scene AP reporter; no Chicago Board of Elections statement found on X; polls closed at 7 p.m. CT

America.title: Fire alarms pulled twice at UT Austin polling site
America.location: Texas Union, University of Texas at Austin, TX
America.summary: UT Austin Police say they are investigating two fire alarm activations Tuesday morning at the Texas Union while it was being used as a polling location. Voting was briefly delayed and resumed about 10 minutes later, and police released an image of a person of interest they believe is unaffiliated with the university.
America.status: Official statement issued by UT Austin Police; investigated as a criminal offense; voting resumed

America.title: Brightspeed internet outage across several states on Election Day
America.summary: Brightspeed's verified account told customers it was experiencing a widespread internet outage affecting many customers, with no estimated time for resolution. An Ohio business carrier says the outage hit the Mansfield area. No impact on election systems has been reported.
America.status: Confirmed by the company in customer replies; no formal restoration notice or cause found on X this sweep

America.title: Bomb threat briefly halted voting at Toledo polling place; voting resumed
America.summary: A bomb threat evacuated the Beverly Elementary School polling location in Toledo on Tuesday morning and temporarily halted voting while police swept the building. Local TV reported the evacuation, and the Lucas County Board of Elections said in a reply on X that the site was back up and voting. Threats also prompted evacuations at other schools in northwest Ohio. 13 Action News now reports that a judge ruled voters assigned to Beverly Elementary may cast a provisional ballot until 9:15 p.m. Tuesday because the threat temporarily closed the site. WLWT's Aaron Thomas, sharing a Lucas County Board of Elections post, says the judge's extension of voting because of the bomb threat may explain the delay in Lucas County results.
America.status: Voting resumed; judge-ordered extension for the affected site; Lucas County results delayed; no device reported found

America.title: Power outage briefly knocked out voting machines at Las Vegas-area vote center
America.location: Desert Breeze Community Center, Clark County, NV
America.summary: A reporter at the Desert Breeze vote center said a bank of voting machines lost power for about 15 minutes, and at least a couple dozen people left saying they would try again later. Clark County's own update covers wait times and says anyone in line by 7 PM can vote; it does not mention the outage.

America.title: Fulton County warns of fake texts about polling-place changes
America.summary: Fulton County said some voters received texts claiming their polling places had moved, and that the county did not send them. Voters can check their polling place on the Georgia Secretary of State's My Voter Page.
America.status: Official statement issued by Fulton County, reported by the AJC

America.title: North Carolina extends voting at five precincts after tech problems
America.summary: The North Carolina State Board of Elections voted to extend voting hours at five precincts in Columbus, Lenoir, Hertford and Wilson counties after computer outages and printer problems delayed voting. CBS 17 and the Hartford Courant report that statewide unofficial results will not post until at least 8:15 PM ET.
America.status: Polls closed statewide at 7:30 PM ET except the five extended precincts, which close as late as 8:15 PM ET

links.label: The North Carolina Beat: polls closed, five precincts extended

America.title: Federal judge orders South Dakota officials to let 'Natives Vote' T-shirt wearer vote
America.summary: Courthouse News reports a federal judge ordered South Dakota officials on Tuesday to allow a Yankton Sioux tribal member wearing a 'Natives Vote' T-shirt to cast a ballot at a polling site. The order resolves a dispute over polling-place attire for that voter; no wider disruption has been reported.
America.status: Court order issued, per Courthouse News; no statement from the South Dakota Secretary of State found on X

America.title: Three Chester County precincts get extended hours
America.summary: Pennsylvania's Department of State says polling hours were extended until 8:30 PM at three precincts in Chester County. The official post doesn't give the reason; unofficial posts attribute it to machine setup problems that delayed opening.
America.status: Official statement issued

America.title: Electrical fire disrupts voting at Germantown polling place
America.summary: KYW Newsradio reports an electrical fire caused a power outage and temporarily disrupted voting at a polling place in Germantown. No post from Philadelphia's election office was found this sweep.
America.status: Early reports; single local outlet

America.title: Phone outage hits some Rhode Island local election offices
America.summary: The Rhode Island Board of Elections says some local election offices are having phone problems because of an outage and directed voters to the state board's line or 2-1-1.
America.status: Official statement issued

America.title: Power outage hit Kansas City polling place; power since restored
America.location: Kansas City, MO (Blue Ridge Church of Christ)
America.summary: A power outage affected voters at the Blue Ridge Church of Christ polling place early Tuesday, and voters were told they could cast ballots at other locations. A KMBC reporter later said power was back on at the site.
America.status: Resolved per local media

America.title: Flooding forces polling place relocations in Florida

America.summary: Brevard County's Supervisor of Elections is temporarily relocating a limited number of precinct polling places because of extreme flooding, and Florida's Secretary of State has published an updated list of polling locations for flood-hit counties. America.title: Brief system issue reported at Broward polling sites

America.title: Flooding in northern Arizona
America.location: Sedona, Oak Creek and Coconino County, Arizona, USA
America.summary: Weekend storms flooded Oak Creek near Sedona and other parts of northern Arizona. The Arizona Emergency Information Network posted local assistance and road-hazard contacts for Coconino County, Flagstaff and Oak Creek. X News summaries report evacuations, road closures and a statewide emergency declaration, which were not confirmed in a linked official post.
America.status: Under investigation

America.title: Bexar County ballot scanner problems during early voting
America.summary: KSAT reported that election judges said some ballots were placed in scanners' emergency compartments during scanner problems at Bexar County early voting sites. The county declined an interview and said it could not provide a statement. The number of affected sites and how long the problems lasted have not been officially confirmed.
America.status: Early reports from local media; no official county statement

Europe.title: Second wave of cyberattacks on supermarket refrigeration
Europe.location: Across Europe, including Belgium, Sweden, Germany, Romania and the UK
Europe.summary: Grocery stores in at least seven European countries saw refrigerator temperatures soar on Monday, and several confirmed a cyberattack similar to one in France three weeks ago. In Belgium, about 40 stores across Delhaize, Carrefour, Spa and other chains were hit, with about €100,000 of food thrown away. BBC reports a huge amount of food dumped in dozens of supermarkets across several countries, and Xinhua says the method matches the October attack in France, where hackers remotely raised temperatures. Security researcher Lukasz Olejnik now lists confirmed victims in Sweden, Belgium, Ireland, Luxembourg, Estonia, the Netherlands, Finland, Portugal, Germany and Italy, with Poland and Romania suspected. Sky News reports a top UK security official says the attacks have also affected the UK meat processing industry. Reuters now reports European supermarkets rushing to patch vulnerabilities, and Channel 4 News says GCHQ is alerting UK companies that could be at risk. AFP reports Germany, Romania and the UK joined the list of countries hit on Tuesday, and Sky News reports new warnings from the UK AI minister and the National Cyber Security Centre. The Hindu now puts the attack at 11 European countries, with store temperatures pushed as high as 50°C, and notes the attackers appear to seek disruption rather than ransom.
Europe.status: Confirmed by several companies and major outlets; UK meat processing impact reported by Sky News; attribution unknown

links.label: AFP: Germany, Romania and UK hit
Channel 4 News: GCHQ alerting UK firms

Europe.title: Cyberattack on French blood service contractor's cold storage
Europe.summary: Le Canard enchaîné reports that on the night of Nov 1–2 hackers attacked a contractor of the Établissement français du sang (EFS), France's blood service, and heated cold rooms holding blood samples, set to stay at minus 30 degrees, up to 110 degrees. FrenchBreaches names the contractor as Coolworld and says the incident was detected in time with no reported operational impact. It resembles the refrigeration attacks on European supermarkets. Update: The Hindu now also reports hackers breached systems to remotely heat EFS freezers holding donor blood samples and plasma.
Europe.status: Reported by Le Canard enchaîné; no EFS statement found on X this sweep; attribution unknown

Europe.title: Moldova suspects a state actor behind cyberattack
Europe.summary: Moldova's prime minister told Euronews the government suspects a state actor is behind a cyberattack. The Euronews post does not detail which systems were hit; unverified posts claim government databases and citizens' ID data were compromised.
Europe.status: Official statement reported by Euronews; scope and attribution under investigation

Europe.title: Bomb threats hit several European flights
Europe.location: Warsaw-Modlin and Warsaw Chopin airports, Poland; Murcia, Spain; Budapest, Hungary
Europe.summary: Bomb threats have now hit at least six passenger flights to Poland, Spain, Bulgaria and Italy. LOT flight LO286 from London diverted to Warsaw-Modlin, and Reuters says Modlin has since reopened. Two Ryanair flights to Rome Fiumicino, from Dublin and Lisbon, were escorted by Italian Air Force jets and searched after landing. Searches so far have found no explosives. The Daily Mail now reports the threats have spread, with multiple flights, including three from the UK, forced to make emergency landings.
Europe.status: No explosives found per reports so far; threats under investigation; no attribution

Europe.title: Violent cost-of-living and anti-government protests
Europe.summary: On Oct 31, masked rioters looted shops in Frankfurt, and German police fired water cannons at youths throwing Molotov cocktails. In Paris and elsewhere in France, police fired tear gas as hundreds of thousands marched against living costs and police violence. In Tirana, protesters threw Molotov cocktails and paving stones at police. Swiss paper Tages-Anzeiger says the riots also reached Switzerland over the weekend, with protests in Zurich. On Tuesday, French students marched through central Paris despite the authorities rejecting their route, Reuters reports, and DW says German officials are looking for those responsible for the Gen Z protest riots.
Europe.status: Confirmed by major outlets; further marches possible

Europe.title: Spyware alerts for German officials
Europe.summary: People who received the alerts were told to treat their phones as compromised. It is not yet known who is behind the attack or how many people were affected.
Europe.status: Under investigation

Europe.title: Poland deploys counterterrorism police near Kaliningrad
Europe.summary: Poland has deployed police counterterrorism units near the Kaliningrad border after intelligence warnings of possible sabotage in the coming days, the Kyiv Independent reports, citing Polish media.
Europe.status: Early reports; no incident reported

Europe.title: Latvia says drones violated its airspace
Europe.summary: Latvia believes one of two drones that violated its airspace was Russian and the other Ukrainian, Reuters reports.
Europe.status: Official assessment reported by Reuters

Europe.title: Germany arrests suspected organizer of Starlink ground station arson in Poland
Europe.location: Reutlingen district, Germany / Wola Krobowska, Poland
Europe.summary: German special police arrested a Turkish national on Nov 3 suspected of ordering the Sept 23 arson attack on a Starlink ground station south of Warsaw, according to a report citing Stuttgart prosecutors. Two alleged perpetrators were arrested in October. Polish prosecutors suspect Russian intelligence involvement, which German authorities have not confirmed.
Europe.status: Arrest reported; investigation ongoing

Russia.title: Russian drone strike sets Odesa's 7th Kilometer market on fire
Russia.summary: Russian drones struck the 7th Kilometer market near Odesa, one of Ukraine's largest wholesale markets, on Wednesday morning, starting a large fire seen on video. One account says the strike came during the working day while the market was busy. No official casualty figures were found in the posts reviewed.
Russia.status: Early reports with video; casualties unknown

Russia.title: Ukrainian drone strike sets Ozon logistics hub in Adygeysk on fire
Russia.summary: A drone attack overnight on November 4 set fire to online retailer Ozon's logistics centre in Adygeysk, damaging the building and partially collapsing its roof, Militarnyi reports. Ozon confirmed the attack and said staff were evacuated, with no casualties reported, and the head of Adygea also confirmed it. Videos posted by OSINT accounts show a large fire at the site.
Russia.status: Confirmed by the company and regional head, per reports; damage still being assessed

Russia.title: 310-drone overnight attack on Ukraine; Zhytomyr largely without power
Russia.location: Kyiv, Zhytomyr, Odesa and other regions, Ukraine
Russia.summary: Russia launched 310 drones overnight into November 4, according to Ukraine's Air Force as cited by journalist Michael Bociurkiw, targeting Kyiv, Dnipro, Poltava, Odesa, Ternopil and the Rivne and Kirovohrad regions. Hromadske Radio reports Zhytomyr remains largely without power after a strike, with electric transport suspended and water facilities on generators. Kyiv Post shows Kyiv in a blackout on generators, and Bociurkiw reports large parts of Odesa without power and Kyiv water only partly restored.
Russia.status: Ongoing; outages continuing

Russia.title: Russian bombing kills 33 at aid point in Komyshuvakha
Russia.summary: Zelenskyy said aerial bombs hit a school in Komyshuvakha, Zaporizhzhia Oblast, where people were receiving humanitarian aid, followed by more bombs on the shelter where people were taking cover. The Kyiv Independent reports at least 33 killed in the Nov 2 strikes, and Zelenskyy said on Nov 3 that more than 50 others may still be trapped under the rubble.
Russia.status: Toll rising; 33 killed per Kyiv Independent citing Zelenskyy; rescue continuing

Russia.title: Massive overnight Russian strike on Ukraine's power grid
Russia.location: Odesa, Cherkasy, Zhytomyr, Vinnytsia, Kharkiv, Dnipro, Chernivtsi, Chernihiv and Rivne regions, Ukraine
Russia.summary: President Zelenskyy says Russia launched 289 attack drones, 17 ballistic missiles and 59 cruise missiles overnight, mainly at power plants and substations across nine regions, and that emergency and unscheduled power outages are ongoing in many cities. He says a strike on a Kharkiv city clinical hospital injured 73 people and damaged its cardiology department. Anton Gerashchenko reports one person killed and at least 17 injured in Dnipro, and NOELreports lists the Ladyzhyn, Prydniprovska, Kryvorizka and Zmiivska thermal power plants as hit. The Kyiv Independent reports that Russian attacks across Ukraine killed 38 people and injured 158, and that a morning missile strike hit hospitals in Dnipro. The Kyiv Independent reports Kyiv now faces emergency power cuts and widespread water outages. The Kyiv Independent calls it Russia's biggest mass attack on Ukraine's energy infrastructure this year. Energy Minister Denys Shmyhal says three drones targeted a substation critical to the stable operation of the Khmelnytskyi Nuclear Power Plant during the attack, and Ukraine has informed the IAEA.
Russia.status: Official statement issued by Ukraine's president; air raid alerts continuing; no Ukrenergo damage assessment found this sweep; customer outage counts not confirmed

links.label: Kyiv Independent: Kyiv emergency power cuts
Liveuamap: Khmelnytskyi NPP substation targeted, per Shmyhal

Russia.title: New overnight Russian drone attack; eastern Kyiv power loss reported
Russia.summary: NOELreports, citing Ukraine's Air Force, says Russia launched 310 drones overnight into Nov. 4, including 81 jet-powered Shaheds, with 272 downed or suppressed and strikes recorded at 19 locations. OSINT account AMK Mapping says almost all of eastern Kyiv lost power overnight after jet-drone strikes on energy infrastructure, including the Kyivska 750 kV substation. The Kyiv outage and substation damage have not yet been confirmed by Ukrenergo, city officials or a major outlet. Update: UkraineWorld reports, citing Ukrenergo, that emergency power cuts in Kyiv cannot yet be lifted and scheduled outage timetables are not in force; drone debris caused fires in two districts.

Russia.title: Emergency alert apps in Ukraine and Russia hacked
Russia.summary: Ukraine and Russia both said their emergency alert apps had been hacked, sending false warnings about air raids and chemical and nuclear attacks. Russia said its app suffered a "massive cyberattack" on Monday, hours after Ukraine reported its own hack. In Ukraine the fake nuclear warning caused unease but not panic. Zelenskyy told PBS NewsHour that Ukraine targeted Russia's emergency alert systems in a retaliatory hack. Hackmanac reports the attacker exploited a flaw in the admin panel of the Russian Emergency Ministry app to push false alerts across 33 regions.
Russia.status: Officially confirmed by both governments; Zelenskyy says Ukraine's hack of Russian alerts was retaliation

Russia.title: Drone strike kills two at Russian-held Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant
Russia.location: Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant, Enerhodar, Ukraine
Russia.summary: The Russian-held Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant says a Ukrainian drone killed two people, including a station employee, Reuters reports. Ukraine's response and any IAEA comment weren't seen in this sweep.
Russia.status: Claim by the Russian-installed plant management, reported by Reuters; not independently confirmed

Russia.title: Ukrainian drone strike reported on Yaroslavl oil refinery
Russia.summary: The Kyiv Independent reports that Ukraine struck the Slavneft-YANOS oil refinery in Yaroslavl with drones overnight on Nov. 3, with residents reporting several fires at the facility, citing Ukrainian monitoring channels. OSINT accounts posted video of fires in the industrial zone, and the independent Russian outlet ASTRA reported explosions in the area. Russian officials had not confirmed damage or casualties at the time of this sweep. Kyiv Post reports the Slavneft-owned refinery caught fire after the drone attack.
Russia.status: Early reports; no official Russian statement yet

Russia.title: Ukrainian drone strike reported on Samara oil facility
Russia.summary: Ukrainian monitoring channels reported that Ukrainian drones struck the Samara Linear Production and Dispatch Station in Prosvet overnight. Kazakhstan reportedly suspended oil pumping through the Atyrau-Samara pipeline after the attack on the Samara hub, with its Energy Ministry cited via TASS.
Russia.status: Strike reported by Ukrainian channels; Kazakh halt reported via TASS and market wires, not yet seen from major Western outlets
